1Password confirms security incident, here’s what you need to know

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (426 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Password management platform 1Password today disclosed a security incident in which an attacker gained access to internal systems and stole select customer account information.
  • 1Password today published a blog post explaining that an attacker “copied a limited amount of customer account information from a subset” of its people, “including the names and email addresses” they use to sign into the platform.
  • According to the company, it began investigating on November 19 after finding indications that an attacker had gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Password management platform 1Password today disclosed a security incident in which an attacker gained access to internal systems and stole select customer account information. Here are the details.

1Password today published a blog post explaining that an attacker “copied a limited amount of customer account information from a subset” of its people, “including the names and email addresses” they use to sign into the platform.

According to the company, it began investigating on November 19 after finding indications that an attacker had gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The attacker then used that account to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, allowing customer account information to be downloaded.

The manufacturer noted that customer vaults were not affected, adding that all vault contents remain secure:.

Although 1Password did not disclose how many customers were affected, saying only that the breach involved “a subset of our customers,” it did specify what information was compromised, including:.

However, 1Password clarified that the exposed invitation and recovery tokens cannot be used to access accounts on their own, as they also require either an SSO sign-in or a verification code sent to the user’s registered email address.

That stated, the manufacturer confirmed that “the attacker also copied source code from private repositories and gained access” to its CI/CD system, which is essentially its DevOps infrastructure used to build, test, and deploy software.

On that point, 1Password noted that its CI/CD system contains “infrastructure related secrets,” and that it has already rotated or revoked all internal credentials that may have been exposed.

The manufacturer also listed other steps it took in response to the incident, including deactivating the compromised GitHub account, tightening internal security controls, and strengthening the verification codes used in account invitations and recovery emails.

Industry observers note that finally, 1Password mentioned users do not need to make any changes to their accounts. Still, it recommended that they remain vigilant against phishing attempts, as attackers can use stolen account information to craft convincing emails, messages, or calls that appear legitimate, particularly those involving account invitations or recovery requests.

Attorneys General Jones and Rayfield File Suit Against SpaceX, Parent Manufacturer of X, xAI, and Grok, Over Creation and Promotion of Child Exploitation and Non-Consensual Images on Platform  Virginia and Oregon Attorneys General seek accountability for harms and significant newly introduced protections for consumers.

***Read the full filing here***.

According to recent reports, RICHMOND, Va. – Today, Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones took a significant step in holding operators of X and its AI tool, Grok, accountable for knowingly failing to protect Virginians, while falsely promoting the safety of its platform and AI tool.

In the lawsuit, the Commonwealth of Virginia alleges that SpaceX, the telecommunications and space transportation conglomerate that operates the social network X and its artificial intelligence tech giant, xAI (now called “SpaceX Super Intelligence”), and developed the Grok family of large language models, failed to prevent Grok from generating sexualized images of people, including children, without their knowledge or consent—while simultaneously promoting the safety of the social media platform and AI tool. The Grok-generated content includes non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII), other non-consensual sexualized images, and Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM). Today’s suit was filed in collaboration with Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield, who filed a separate but similar action.

Recent findings suggest that “This lawsuit is about seeking justice for the millions of Virginians who maintain accounts on X and were misled by the firm’s false reassurances that their data and images would be safe on the platform,” remarked Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones. “When xAI allowed Grok’s creators to sideline consent to turn a profit, they prioritized growth and engagement over safety, and they deceived the public about it. Today’s filings are the first step towards holding this company accountable.”.

In a recent development, with a single existing photograph, Grok could, and did, fabricate a realistic image or video of a person nude, or partially nude, or engaged in sexual activity, all without the individual’s knowledge or consent. This violation is not acceptable.

The company ignored industry-standard safeguards so xAI could distinguish itself in the AI arms race. Grok’s ability to generate sexualized content was leveraged as a promotional opportunity. These exploitations of Virginian’s safety enabled the widespread creation and distribution of sexualized images through Grok’s integration with X.

Recent findings suggest that “SpaceX allowed Grok and the X platform to create, host, and share unacceptable and dangerous content—and in fact knowingly designed a product without the obviously necessary safeguards in place,” remarked Attorney General Rayfield. “It’s no surprise that Grok and X became a haven for perpetrators using AI to create and share child sexual abuse material. The lack of needed safety measures was considered a feature, not a bug, which they promoted as ‘spicy mode.’”.

According to recent reports, in his filing, Attorney General Jones shows that SpaceX and its subsidiaries marketed Grok as an AI companion with a “rebellious streak,” knowing that its video and image generation technology would be used to produce CSAM, non-consensual intimate images of adults and children (NCII), and other sexualized imagery. In fact, X and its subsidiaries created and promoted a “spicy mode” that specifically allowed for the creation of nude and otherwise sexualized images.

Industry observers note that A study by the Center for Countering Digital Harm (“CCDH”) estimated that, between December 29, 2025, and January 8, 2026, Grok created and posted on X approximately three million sexualized images, including approximately 23,000 images that appeared to depict children. That’s an average pace of roughly 190 sexualized images per minute, and one sexualized image of a child approximately every 41 seconds. Nearly 30% of the sexualized images of children identified by CCDH in its study remained publicly accessible in posts on X a week or more after they were identified—and even many of those that were “removed” could still be accessed via separate URLs.

SpaceX and its subsidiaries publicly assured consumers that robust protections were in place to prevent Grok from creating CSAM, NCII, and other sexualized images. In reality, millions of people — including in Oregon and Virginia — were nevertheless exposed to harmful content and the risk that their own images could be manipulated into sexually explicit content without their consent.

“Time and again, xAI and X told consumers they were being protected from abuses. That was false. Instead, the tool permitted people to routinely create and circulate non-consensual intimate imagery and sexualized images, and child sexual abuse material (CSAM), causing harm to individuals and children,” added Attorney General Jones. “Companies that deploy powerful tools don’t get to ignore consumer safety and call it innovation. The law applies to everyone, and this office will hold big tech accountable when they break the law.”.

“Like the other technology companies that we’re holding accountable, xAI not only knowingly endangered kids and our communities, but they also lied to our faces about non-existent safety measures,” added Attorney General Rayfield.

According to recent reports, attorney General Jones’ lawsuit was filed in the Circuit Court for the City of Richmond. Attorney General Rayfield’s lawsuit was filed in Multnomah County Circuit Court.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that popular AI dictation app Wispr Flow is rolling out a fresh speech-to-text model for Mac, iPhone, and other platforms, promising fewer transcription errors and better recognition of names and technical terms. Here are the details.

Wispr Flow this week released Canto-2, its newest speech-to-text model, which the firm says reduces transcription errors by 36% across 14 languages and by more than 15% in English compared to its predecessor, Canto-1.

In practice, that means the average error rate dropped from 9.9% to 6.3% across the 14 languages, and from 3.2% to 2.7% in English, according to Wispr’s internal benchmarks.

According to the firm, teaching a model to recognize specific names and terms comes with a trade-off: the more it relies on that user-specific context, the more likely it is to insert those words even when they weren’t actually spoken.

Wispr notes that Canto-2 strikes a better balance between context and accuracy, improving its ability to recognize user-specific terms without substantially increasing the frequency of incorrect substitutions:.

Canto-2 recovers hard names and terms accurately nearly 7 of 10 times, without more false insertions. It makes a third fewer mistakes across 14 languages, and has the lowest Hindi error rate of any multilingual model on Hugging Face’s open benchmark. It is 10 times the scale of Canto-1, and our biggest step yet toward dictation that’s ready to send without a single edit.

According to the company, the percentage of difficult names and terms correctly recognized went from 41% to 69% between Canto-1 and Canto-2, “without inserting them more often.” It added that this improvement holds up even as the user’s custom dictionary grows, with the fresh model correctly recognizing 92% of easier terms even with 1,000 saved entries.

Wispr also noted that it trained Canto-2 to handle real-world dictation conditions, including background noise, laptop and phone microphones, and sentences that restart halfway through, rather than relying solely on clean recordings of scripted speech.

When tested using Hugging Face’s public multilingual benchmark, Canto-2 achieved results that would have placed it third overall as of November 9. However, Wispr conducted the evaluation itself, and the model has not yet been officially added to the leaderboard as of today, November 25.

In its own internal benchmarks, the company indicates Canto-2 achieved the lowest average error rate among the competing models it tested across 14 languages.

Canto-2 is now available to Wispr Flow people on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android in the Americas, with the rollout to other regions underway.

  • As reported by the South China Morning Post, Apple has pulled MiniMax’s chatbot Talkie from the App Store worldwide, after reports that “the AI companion app sent inappropriate messages to minors.”.
  • MiniMax is one of China’s leading AI companies, offering a range of generative AI products ranging from its flagship M-series language models to the Hailuo AI video generation platform.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following reports that its characters sent inappropriate messages to minors, Apple has removed the popular Chinese AI companion app Talkie from the App Store. Here are the details.

As reported by the South China Morning Post, Apple has pulled MiniMax’s chatbot Talkie from the App Store worldwide, after reports that “the AI companion app sent inappropriate messages to minors.”.

MiniMax is one of China’s leading AI companies, offering a range of generative AI products ranging from its flagship M-series language models to the Hailuo AI video generation platform.

Recent findings suggest that in 2023, the Shanghai-based company released Talkie through Subsup, a Singaporean subsidiary. According to Chinese research firm Unique Research, Talkie had “almost 11 million monthly active people across its website and app as of October,” the South China Morning Post notes.

Now, however, the app is facing scrutiny following a joint investigation by the UK-based Bureau of Investigative Journalism and Australian broadcaster ABC News, which found that Talkie’s AI-generated characters allegedly engaged in inappropriate interactions with minors, including “degrading language, possessive behaviour and romantic role-play.”.

According to the Bureau of Investigative Journalism, in addition to inappropriate romantic interactions, the investigation uncovered conversations involving verbal abuse, violence, and controlling behavior.

In one case, a chatbot told a 12-year-old girl: “You’re a pathetic waste of space and you’ll never amount to anything.”.

The investigation also documented the experiences of two sisters, aged 10 and 13, whose mother discovered more than 40 conversations with Talkie characters involving violence, aggressive behavior, and attempts to control girls.

To make matters worse, the investigation also raised concerns about how Talkie handles users’ personal data, including their conversations with AI characters.

Following the investigation, Apple confirmed that it had removed Talkie from App Stores worldwide for including sexual content, “though it did not say whether this related to sexual content served to minors,” the South China Morning Post noted.

According to recent reports, ironically, the report also notes that Talkie saw a sharp decline in downloads amid complaints about stricter age verification measures introduced in recent months. According to Unique Research, newly introduced downloads fell by 32.2% in October compared to the previous month.

Today’s news comes amid increasing scrutiny of AI chatbots, particularly their potential risks in interactions with minors.

Earlier this year, Elon Musk’s Grok faced widespread criticism after users exploited its image-generation capabilities to create sexualized images of real people, including minors.

Apple never pulled X or Grok from the App Store, though it did threaten to remove the latter unless xAI addressed violations of its App Store guidelines.

Meanwhile, Character.AI has faced multiple lawsuits over its chatbots’ interactions with minors, including one filed by a mother who alleged that one of its chatbots contributed to her 14-year-old son’s suicide.

Coincidentally, Character AI also made headlines today after a coalition of 42 US attorneys general challenged the company’s prepares to auction off its platform and the private conversations of more than 21 million US accounts (including 2.1 million registered to minors) as part of its bankruptcy proceedings.

Yesterday, Fresh York Governor Kathy Hochul signed legislation imposing a five-year ban on the manufacturing, distribution, and sale of toys with built-in AI chatbots, including dolls, stuffed animals, and robots capable of holding conversations with children.

The law, which takes effect in February 2027, is aimed at protecting children from potentially harmful interactions with AI.

Take a look at Proton’s Black Friday offers, starting at $1.99 per month.

The problem with strong passwords isn’t understanding why you need them; it’s keeping track of a different one for every account.

That’s useful whether you’re creating an account for a single purchase or signing into a service you use every day.

In a recent development, unique passwords also help limit the fallout from a data breach. If a retailer exposes your login credentials, using a different password elsewhere means those same credentials won’t unlock your other accounts.

With unlimited logins and encrypted vaults that sync across devices, Proton Pass lets you keep those details together as you move between your phone and computer.

In a recent development, proton Pass is available for practically every platform, from Chrome and Firefox on the web to native macOS, Windows, and Linux apps to, of course, iOS and Android. This makes it trivially easy to access your passwords, passkeys, and API credentials wherever you find yourself.

Black Friday shopping often leaves something behind long after the packages arrive: a steady stream of promotional emails from stores you barely remember visiting.

Proton Pass includes unlimited hide-my-email aliases, giving you an alternative to handing out your real address every time you create an account.

An alias is an extra email address that forwards messages to your normal inbox. You can give it to a shopping website and still receive your order confirmations and delivery updates, without sharing the underlying address you use for everything else.

If that alias starts receiving spam, you can switch it off. Your real email address stays the same, and you don’t have to update all your other accounts.

It’s a practical way to put some distance between your primary inbox and the websites you’re trying for the first time. A separate alias for each service also gives you more control: you can stop messages arriving through one address without disrupting the others.

Passwords are only part of what’s worth keeping in a secure, accessible place.

Proton Pass also stores notes, credit card details, and other confidential information in end-to-end encrypted vaults. That makes it useful for the small, everyday moments when you need something sensitive and don’t want to go looking for it.

When you’re booking a flight, saved passport details let you look up the information you need without digging through a drawer halfway through the reservation.

When you’re shopping online, saved card details mean you don’t have to leave the checkout page to find your wallet.

Industry observers note that when you’re traveling, keeping a digital copy of an vital document within reach gives you a convenient reference while you’re away from home. It doesn’t replace an original document where one is required, but it can save you from searching through scattered files and messages.

Industry observers note that pass Plus also includes a built-in two-factor authenticator, Dark Web Monitoring, and secure link and vault sharing. Those features give you more ways to manage access to your accounts and share sensitive information when you need to.

Pass Plus is the straightforward choice for one person who wants password generation, autofill, unlimited aliases, and secure storage.

It has been revealed that pass Family includes six Pass Plus accounts and a family admin panel. If several people in your household need a password manager, it’s worth considering rather than setting everyone up with separate subscriptions.

Sources indicate that proton Unlimited bundles Pass with Proton VPN, Proton Mail, Proton Drive, and more, including 500 GB of cloud storage. It’s the option to consider if you also want a VPN, encrypted email, and cloud storage alongside your password manager.

A password manager isn’t the most conspicuous Black Friday purchase, but it’s one you can put to work immediately: the next account you create, the next password you forget, or the next time a checkout asks for details you don’t have handy.

As is now usual, the company has created some exclusive wallpaper to mark the event, and you can download it for iPhone, iPad, and Mac ….

The store will be the seventh one to open in India. There’s no press release or photos as yet – the organization has simply quietly added the store to its list in the country.

As we’ve previously explained, Apple had been trying to open retail stores in India since at least 2015, but had to undertake a lengthy battle with the government before finally being allowed to do so in 2023. Since then, the company has averaged two upcoming stores a year.

According to recent reports, india has taken a clever approach to economic development, offering both incentives to establish local manufacturing plants, and barriers to imports of foreign-made products. That carrot-and-stick approach has proven successful, with companies like Apple jumping through the necessary hoops in order to sell their products to the second largest population in the world.

An India First initiative required companies to manufacture a significant proportion of their products within the country in order to avoid high import tariffs. This forced Apple, Samsung, and other companies to establish manufacturing plants in India, bringing jobs to the country.

It has been revealed that additionally, India does not allow organization-branded retail stores unless the same conditions are met. That particular requirement was mostly intended to target Apple.

Recent findings suggest that the strategy worked, with Apple asking its suppliers and iPhone assemblers to establish manufacturing plants within India. Initially, that was just for the iPhone SE, but more advanced phones have gradually been added, and today the country is the second largest manufacturing base after China. All iPhones sold in the US are made in India.

Apple has for some time now created unique wallpapers to mark the opening of each new store, and the latest example is particularly beautiful.

Sources indicate that to download it, you need to visit this page on the device for which you want to use it. For example, if you visit the page on a Mac, you will automatically be taken to the desktop version.

#166936. A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (621 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct.
  • Recent findings suggest that however, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive.
  • It has been revealed that buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct. 6. The market despises uncertainty, and losing a visionary founder, particularly one without a well-telegraphed succession initiative, makes it worse.

Recent findings suggest that however, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive. Trading in the $160s, Nvidia's valuation has taken a massive haircut, yet its underlying business fundamentals remain largely intact. While Huang was the architect of Nvidia's AI dominance, the firm's moat — superior GPUs, the CUDA software ecosystem, and networking expertise — does not walk out the door with him. The company's structural advantage in the global artificial intelligence rollout persists.

It has been revealed that buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options. Huang's departure guarantees that Nvidia will be operating under a cloud of transition for the foreseeable future. Executing a permanent CEO search while navigating global regulatory scrutiny takes time. Consequently, Nvidia's implied volatility (IV)—the market's pricing of expected future price swings — has spiked to highs not seen since the tariff tantrum in the first half of 2025, and this elevated IV is highly likely to persist for several months as the leadership drama slowly unfolds.

This prolonged period of high implied volatility can be a goldmine for option sellers, specifically those executing options overlays such as covered call strategies. When you buy NVDA shares at these depressed levels and simultaneously sell out-of-the-money call options against your position, the premiums you collect are directly tied to IV. Because fear and transition-related uncertainty have dramatically inflated these option prices, the income generated from selling covered calls is now significantly higher than usual.

This lowers the risk profile of holding the stock considerably over time. Consistently collecting these inflated premiums systematically lowers your overall cost basis in the underlying shares. If the stock trades sideways or recovers slowly during the CEO search, you are generating an outsized cash yield on a stagnant asset. If the stock experiences further downside turbulence, the heavy premium income acts as a substantial downside buffer, meaningfully reducing the strategy's overall risk over time.

By deploying a persistent covered call strategy, investors can leverage the exact fear driving the stock down to generate robust, risk-reducing income while maintaining exposure to the undeniable future of AI.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that with most AI chatbots using your interactions as training data, we’ve previously cautioned against sharing sensitive personal details with them, highlighting the much stronger privacy protections offered by Apple.
  • The company recently filed for bankruptcy and is now offering all of its assets for sale, including the contents of user chat sessions.
  • Industry observers note that character․AI had long come under fire for its extremely irresponsible attitude to privacy and safety.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that with most AI chatbots using your interactions as training data, we’ve previously cautioned against sharing sensitive personal details with them, highlighting the much stronger privacy protections offered by Apple. If you ever needed evidence of the importance of this, the Character․ai mess provides it.

The company recently filed for bankruptcy and is now offering all of its assets for sale, including the contents of user chat sessions. Some 42 state attorneys general are trying to block this, but it’s unclear whether they will succeed ….

Industry observers note that character․AI had long come under fire for its extremely irresponsible attitude to privacy and safety. Last summer, it was accused of harvesting mental health data from underage owners, and in May of this year it faced a lawsuit after its chatbots were found to be pretending to be licensed doctors. The company filed for bankruptcy last month.

A group of 42 attorneys general are trying to block the chatbot company from auctioning off owners’ chat histories and other sensitive information […] “Nothing in the agreement restricts what the buyer may do with the data after closing, including selling it,” the AGs say in a court filing […].

“Character․AI’s plan to auction off its platform, including the IP addresses and private chats histories of its owners — many of them children — with zero protection for those users is appalling,” California Attorney General Rob Bonta noted in a statement. “If this sale goes through, users’ sensitive data would go into the hands of a buyer even though Character․AI promised consumers that their data would not be sold.”.

The chat histories reportedly include conversations in which AI characters drew both adults and children into explicit sexual conversations.

Siri AI interactions are handled on-device wherever possible. Where this isn’t possible, Private Cloud Compute (PCC) servers are used, with guarantees that no data is stored or linked to your Apple account. Apple has designed the system in such a way that its privacy claims can be independently verified by security researchers.

Industry observers note that when a user makes a request, Apple Intelligence analyzes whether it can be processed on device. For more complex requests, it can draw on Private Cloud Compute, which extends the privacy and security of your iPhone into the cloud. With Private Cloud Compute, only the data that is relevant to your request is processed on Apple silicon servers, before being removed.

According to recent reports, the data being processed in Private Cloud Compute is not stored or made accessible to Apple. It is processed only to fulfill your request, after which point the results are returned securely to your device and are not retained by Private Cloud Compute. Independent privacy and security researchers can inspect the code that runs on Apple silicon servers that enable Private Cloud Compute to verify this privacy promise at any time.

Sources indicate that apple also recently introduced a safe way to ask an AI questions about your health. Data sources used are limited to the same platforms used by healthcare professionals, with links to peer-reviewed clinical citations. Apple guarantees that your chat sessions are not used for AI training with no retention of either questions or answers.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that apple’s Mac lineup is stronger than ever this year, largely thanks to the new MacBook Neo.
  • Recent findings suggest that the MacBook Neo is Apple’s most affordable laptop ever, starting at $699 (presently on sale for $599).
  • It has been revealed that unlike Apple’s other Macs, the MacBook Neo is powered by an A-series chip rather than an M-series chip.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that apple’s Mac lineup is stronger than ever this year, largely thanks to the new MacBook Neo. If you’re deciding between the MacBook Neo and the MacBook Air this holiday season, here’s everything you need to know.

Recent findings suggest that the MacBook Neo is Apple’s most affordable laptop ever, starting at $699 (presently on sale for $599). It features a solid aluminum design that comes in a range of fun colors, including Silver, Blush, Citrus, and Indigo.

It has been revealed that unlike Apple’s other Macs, the MacBook Neo is powered by an A-series chip rather than an M-series chip. It uses the A18 Pro chip originally introduced with the iPhone 16 Pro, featuring a 6-core CPU and 5-core GPU.

In a recent development, the MacBook Neo comes with 8GB of unified memory, with no additional RAM configuration options available. It starts with 256GB of storage, with a 512GB configuration available for an additional $100. That $100 upgrade also gets you Touch ID, which is not included in the base model.

There are some other trade-offs compared to the MacBook Air. The MacBook Neo lacks a backlit keyboard, MagSafe charging, and a Force Touch trackpad. It also has more limited USB-C connectivity and supports just one external display.

Recent findings suggest that still, the MacBook Neo offers an impressive feature set. It has a 13-inch display, up to 16 hours of battery life, a 1080p FaceTime camera, and the full macOS experience.

Industry observers note that the MacBook Air, meanwhile, was updated earlier this year with Apple’s M5 chip. It starts at $1,299, making it $600 more expensive than the entry-level MacBook Air. The MacBook Air is currently on sale with a starting price of $999.

For that $600 upgrade, the MacBook Air offers several key advantages over the MacBook Air. The M5 chip has a 10-core CPU and up to a 10-core GPU, enabling better sustained performance than the MacBook Neo.

Industry observers note that the MacBook Air also starts with 16GB of unified memory and 512GB of storage, both double the entry-level MacBook Neo. You can configure it with up to 32GB of memory and 4TB of storage, while the MacBook Neo is limited to 8GB of memory and 512GB of storage.

Apple rates the MacBook Air for up to 18 hours of video streaming and 15 hours of wireless web browsing, compared to 16 hours and 11 hours, respectively, for the MacBook Neo.

As I wrote in my review earlier this year, I think the MacBook Neo is a great Mac, full stop … not just because of the great price. It can handle the vast majority of things most people will throw at it. This includes web browsing, basic photo and video editing, research, and much more.

Industry observers note that the M5 MacBook Air, meanwhile, offers more power and more configuration options. This makes it a great option for people who need more storage, RAM, and power than the MacBook Neo can offer.

One of my favorite things about the MacBook Air is that it’s available in two screen sizes. The 15-inch MacBook Air is one of my favorite Apple laptops with a combination of the ultra-thin and light design and the larger screen. I think a lot of people forget it exists, but it’s an excellent choice.

Industry observers note that to recap, I think the MacBook Neo is a great choice for everyday tasks like web browsing, email, writing, and streaming. The MacBook Air is a better fit for more demanding workflows, including photo and video editing, coding, working with large spreadsheets, and heavy multitasking.

Industry observers note that beyond performance, the MacBook Air offers a handful of niceties that you won’t find on the MacBook Neo. These include a backlit keyboard, a larger display with True Tone, MagSafe charging, a better webcam and speakers, and a Force Touch trackpad. It also includes Touch ID on every configuration, longer battery life, and support for two external displays.

It has been revealed that if it’s in the budget, I think the MacBook Air is an excellent choice for all Mac shoppers. It’s plenty powerful, thin and light, and is highly configurable compared to the MacBook Neo.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Now it all has been patched up in my fork of FreeBee:.
  • It’s all in a pull request to Phil’s upstream FreeBee, still open: https://github.com/philpem/freebee/pull/57, and the CPU fix in one to his Musashi.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

(This is a guest post by Tenox).

Industry observers note that the AT&T UNIX PC, aka PC 7300 aka 3B1, is a 1985 Unix desktop developed by Convergent Technologies and sold by AT&T. Emulating it is nothing latest. Phil Pemberton started FreeBee in 2010, and Neozeed has covered it here since: booting the diagnostic disk in 2011, booting AT&T UNIX in 2014 thanks to Andrew Warkentin, and running the C compiler in 2020 thanks to shadyjesse. Arnold Robbins added bigger disks and keeps the 3B1 software alive at skeeve.com/3b1. However there was no networking, and the mouse had to be grabbed with F10.

Now it all has been patched up in my fork of FreeBee:.

It’s all in a pull request to Phil’s upstream FreeBee, still open: https://github.com/philpem/freebee/pull/57, and the CPU fix in one to his Musashi.

Industry observers note that the ultimate UNIX PC image! UNIX System V 3.51m with Fix Disk 2.0 and 187 packages: nearly every program made for the UNIX PC, like Microsoft Word, Multiplan, dBASE III, WordStar 2000, GCC 2.5.8, GNU Emacs 19, TeX and over 80 games. It comes from THE STORE!, the 3B1 archive and the disk images of Arnold Robbins, Alain Knaff and the VCF. Credit is due!

Behold! UNIX System V 3.51m and the Office on an emulated AT&T UNIX PC:.

Specs: AT&T UNIX PC (3B1), 68010 at 10 MHz (10x here), 4 MB RAM, 720x348 one-bit screen, 195 MB disk, 3B1 Ethernet board.

Everything runs in windows that you move, resize and overlap with the mouse, even the system panels:.

The Demonstration Programs are pure eye candy:.

Industry observers note that there are productivity apps too! Microsoft Word and Multiplan take the full screen:.

Now some newly introduced stuff, made in 2026 for this image!

Recent findings suggest that new Games! 2048, Bubble Breaker, Falling Blocks, Snake and Sokoban, all AI generated, as native 3B1 windows in the Office:.

Sources indicate that telnetu! The old WIN/TCP telnet chokes on today’s servers, so I wrote a upcoming one with its own VT100/xterm terminal, UTF-8 and DNS, full screen or in windows: https://github.com/tenox7/telnetu.

Archaic! A tiny web browser for WRP, which renders the page on a modern computer and sends it as a picture with clickable links: https://github.com/tenox7/archaic.

Industry observers note that bonus: the tall screen! Just for fun I patched FreeBee, the kernel, the window driver and the shared library to run at 720×696. It’s a super hacky hack, so it has its own branch and image:.

According to recent reports, as usual I have prepared a ready to run, portable image with FreeBee binaries for macOS (Apple Silicon), Linux (x64 and arm64) and Windows (x64). Just unpack and run run.sh (or run.cmd on Windows). At “Please login:” type tenox for the Office, or root for a shell. There are no passwords. For Archaic, start WRP on your computer first.

Download: https://files.42718.net/mirror/tenox/os/att/3b1/virt/att3b1-unix351-freebee.tar.lz.

Tall screen: https://files.42718.net/mirror/tenox/os/att/3b1/virt/att3b1-unix351-freebee-tallhack.tar.lz.

Source (FreeBee, my fork): https://github.com/tenox7/freebee.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Whether you're ready to dive headfirst into the Christmas spirit or craving something heavier, this weekend's lineup has you covered. We've got a cozy, second-chance holiday rom-com adapted from a beloved Jill Shalvis novel, an intimate Spanish drama starring Belén Cuesta and Karra Elejalde about a community coping with a devastating 1980s tragedy, and a moody, Vincent Cassel-led French period piece that reimagines the legend of Quasimodo amid the turmoil of 1830s Paris.

Industry observers note that that should keep you busy through the umpteenth helping of leftover stuffing, yeah? Here are three new-to-Netflix movies to add to your weekend watchlist.

Sure, we've got a few more days until December arrives, but if you want to get into the holiday spirit early, a yuletide rom-com is an easy entry point. Based on the second of the Heartbreaker Bay novels by Jill Shalvis, this Christmastime romance centers on San Francisco pet shop owner Willa Davis (Rachel Melvin), who, a decade after Keane Winters (Thomas Beaudoin) stood her up in high school, re-encounters the fella who slighted her when he comes into her shop in need of a cat sitter for the holidays.

Recent findings suggest that though Willa still harbors a grudge, she unexpectedly falls for Keane — even though he doesn't remember hurting her all those years ago. Directed by Ashley Avis, the 2017 film also stars Flo Lawrence, Alexandra Weaver, and Annie Thurman.

Watch "The Trouble with Mistletoe" on Netflix now.

Inspired by a real-world tragedy — the October 1980 gas explosion at the Marcelino Ugalde public school in Ortuella, Spain — this Spanish drama stars Belén Cuesta and Karra Elejalde as Mariaje and Nicasio, respectively, a mother and grandfather whose lives are irreversibly changed after losing nine-year-old Nuco (Alex Infantes) in a gas explosion at his school.

Based on the novel of the same name by Fernando Aramburu and adapted by writer-director Mariano Barroso, "The Child" weaves a fictional story around the real-life tragedy, showing how not only individuals have to grapple with their personal grief and loss but also Whole communities and, in the case of Spain, entire countries.

Watch "The Child" on Netflix now.

You already know Victor Hugo's "The Hunchback of Notre-Dame," but while that classic French tale is famously set in 15th-century Paris, this Netflix adaptation moves up the action to 1830 on the eve of the July Revolution, around when Hugo himself published his most famous work.

Sources indicate that as political turmoil and cholera threaten to ravage the City of Light, a hunchbacked stonemason named Quasimodo (played by César winner Vincent Cassel), believed to resist the disease, is hunted down by police for medical experiments. Things get even more complicated when Quasimodo falls for a dancer named Agnès (Daphné Patakia), an unrequited love that leads the hunchback to risk everything to keep her safe.

Watch "The Hunchback, Soul of Paris" on Netflix now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 28 is coming next year, and a new rumor claims the upgrade will “revamp the iPhone’s notification system.” This comes as Android has introduced features like “Notification Organizer” to help owners sort notifications into different categories.

Sources indicate that 9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Score Sony’s INZONE noise-canceling earbuds for 38% off. These deliver immersive 360 Spatial Sound, active noise canceling, low-latency wireless connectivity, and much more.

Recent findings suggest that the report cites “multiple sources” and comes from MacRumors. There aren’t any specific details about what changes iOS 28 will introduce for notifications. “The sources said iOS 28 will include significant changes to Notification Center, but we do not have any specific details,” the report says.

The iOS notifications system is overdue for an revision. While Apple has added features like Apple Intelligence-based priority notifications and notification summaries, the system still lacks other organization and sorting settings.

Android 16 introduced several significant notification changes, focused primarily on reducing clutter and prioritizing notable information. For Pixel devices, the upgrade also introduced Notification Organizer, a feature that automatically groups and silences low-priority alerts, including promotions, news, and social media notifications.

As Abner explained on 9to5Google last year:.

The Notification Organizer will sort your alerts into the following categories: Promotions, News, Social, and Suggested. The first two are already on, but you must enable the remaining ones. There’s also an option to “Always expand bundles.”.

Industry observers note that I’d love for Apple to adopt a similar system on iPhone, iPad, and Mac. Even with the recent Apple Intelligence additions, the iOS notifications system is still far too basic.

According to recent reports, most impressive for me are the deals we're seeing on flagships. The Apple AirPods Max 2 from are reduced from $549 to $419 at Amazon. That's $130 off this year's model! Likewise, the Sony WH-1000XM6 have seen a hefty discount, dropping from $459 to $348 at Amazon.

In our Sony WH-CH530 review, we gave these plucky little cans a full five stars. Why? Because look at that $69 MSRP. That's why. For the money, these cans offer stellar sound, plenty of comfort, solid battery life and fun colorways! And now they're just $38.

The Skullcandy Crusher Evo literally have a bass slider in them to make your head wobble! So if it's bass you're after, and you fancy $120 off, this one's for you.

It has been revealed that there was only one thing we didn't like in our Sony WH-CH730N review, and that was the U.S. MSRP of $199. Well, that's changed with this deal. For $99, the WH-CH730N are a hell of a lot of headphones for the money.

Great fit, finish, sound and noise cancelling — the JBL Live 780NC are some impressive mid-range cans. And this Black Friday deal makes them even better.

According to recent reports, the venerable Beats Studio Pro. but this time... $200 off MSRP! Solid ANC? Check. A cool, stylish look? Check. Good sound quality? This isn't a deal to pass up.

Bose might have replaced the QuietComfort headphones with a newer (also reduced) pair, but at this price, the OG QuietComforts are still a super tempting deal. Excellent ANC, a comfortable fit, and increasingly-rare-these-days physical controls.

The Nothing Headphone (1) certainly look the part, and can help you live out your Cyberpunk dreams while offering solid customizable sound and a great control scheme.

It has been revealed that these may have been succeeded by the Momentum 5, but that doesn't make them any less impressive, especially given this massive $120 saving. The Sennheiser Momentum 4 are seriously good value at this price.

Sony recently relaunched the original XM4, hence the XM4C. These updated cans now have Bluetooth 6.0, a fresh removable and replaceable battery, and some AI audio upscaling. The XM4 were still fantastic anyway — even in 2026. But new features is never a bad thing, and nor is $101 off.

Remember earlier when I said Bose had replaced the original QuietComforts? Well, the new ones are right here and also on sale at $160 off! If you want some snazzier colors but similarly powerful ANC and that warm Bose sound, you've found the cans for you — the Bose QuietComfort Headphones 2nd gen.

Sources indicate that these Sonos cans earned an impressive 4.5 stars in our Sonos Ace review. The sound and noise cancelling were on point, as was the battery life, the design and the integration with other Sonos gear. And now they're $120 off!

Recent findings suggest that the Beats 360 are the latest in the Beats range (seriously, they only launched like 2 months ago) and ideal for working out. They're water- and sweatproof, and they feature replaceable ear and head pads. That means you can choose the most comfortable pads for your workout, and swap out if they get gross from, well, your sweaty self.

Sony's XM6 are the latest flagships. They weigh very little and sound excellent — and now you can get them for $100 off. As you'll see in our Sony WH-1000XM6 review, they offer excellent noise cancellation, improved call quality over prior models, and an epic 30 hours of battery life. Flagship quality, and now mid-range price.

It has been revealed that sheer elegance and class. That's how I'd describe the Bowers & Wilkins Px7 S3. I actually own and use a set of these on a near daily basis at home. The Px7 S3 have a warmer, bassier tune than the reference-y Px8 S2 (also on sale), but you still get that Bowers refinement and fidelity.

According to recent reports, another flagship drop! The AirPods Max 2 drop have dropped a little lower before now to $399, but not by much. And given these are the latest flagships from Apple no less, $130 is a surprisingly good chunk of cash off.

Recent findings suggest that as well as the Px7 S3, I also own the Px8 S2. So I'm pretty well place to dispense some sage advice here: buy the Px8 S2. No, seriously, you won't regret it. I know, I know: they're pricey, but they make up for it in spades with beautiful, spacious, high fidelity sound, plus exquisite build quality and strong ANC.

#166923. Judge orders Apple to produce 3,200 documents in Epic Games dispute

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (902 w)

Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 9to5mac ↗ Open Full Page

Judge orders Apple to produce 3,200 documents in Epic Games dispute

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (902 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A federal judge has ordered Apple to produce a random sample of 3,200 documents for Epic Games to review, following Epic’s allegations that Apple improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions.
  • With Apple and Epic trading arguments in the Supreme Court over whether the civil contempt ruling against Apple should stand, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.
  • In August, Apple submitted its proposal to the district court, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A federal judge has ordered Apple to produce a random sample of 3,200 documents for Epic Games to review, following Epic’s allegations that Apple improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions. Here are the details.

With Apple and Epic trading arguments in the Supreme Court over whether the civil contempt ruling against Apple should stand, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.

In August, Apple submitted its proposal to the district court, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%. Epic, however, is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.

Earlier this month, Epic accused Apple of improperly withholding more than 122,000 documents matching a set of search terms agreed upon by both companies to help identify documents that could shed light on how Apple arrived at those rates.

[…] Apple is withholding well over 99% of the documents returned by running the agreed-to search terms on the files of the four custodians Apple notes decided on the proposed fee (Tim Cook, Eddy Cue, Carson Oliver, and Kevan Parekh (Apple’s new CFO)) and three other key individuals (Nate Barton, Alex Roman, and Phil Schiller). Apple claims these withheld documents are not relevant to this proceeding-even though they hit on case-specific terms such as “proffer,” “contempt,” “injunction,” and “link-out.” To put this into context, while Apple produced 632 custodial documents returned by these search terms (including families), Apple is withholding over 122,000 based on a claim of non-responsiveness.

Apple, in turn, pushed back against Epic’s accusations, saying the search terms were overly broad and had captured large numbers of documents unrelated to the proceedings.

[…] at least 95% of the Initial Custodian Document Population hit on generic terms […]. These sweeping terms do not just increase the total volume of the Initial Custodian Document Population, they also captured highly sensitive and irrelevant documents, such as Apple employees’ personal tax or financial records, medical records, documents discussing unannounced products, documents containing passwords, investor-relations materials, and privileged or protected legal communications.

The company also asked the court to reject Epic’s motion to order it to produce all non-privileged documents matching the agreed-upon search terms, and alternatively suggested submitting a randomized, statistically significant sample of the documents it deemed nonresponsive to a Special Master for independent review.

As it turns out, neither firm got exactly what it originally wanted, but the judge ruled largely in Epic’s favor on how to determine whether Apple had improperly withheld documents.

Following a hearing in which both companies presented their respective proposals for how a randomized sampling of the documents should be conducted, Magistrate Judge Thomas S. Hixson decided to adopt Epic’s proposal, which called for Apple to produce a random sample of 3,200 documents it had previously deemed nonresponsive, along with their associated document families, for Epic itself to review.

All documents in the sample will be drawn from the files of the seven Apple custodians referenced in Epic’s original motion.

Apple, by contrast, had suggested a considerably smaller sample of 383 documents, arguing that this would be statistically significant at a 95% confidence level.

In his decision, Judge Hixson agreed that Epic had legitimate reasons to question Apple’s reasons for withholding the documents:.

It has been revealed that apple’s responsiveness rate is so dramatically low that it raises red flags. With Apple screening out more than 99% of the documents that hit on the agreed search terms, it is unreasonable to ask Epic to believe that Apple is making these responsiveness calls in good faith. That is particularly true in this case, in which Judge Gonzalez Rogers has sanctioned Apple for its large-scale abuse of the attorney-client privilege for the purpose of obscuring the evidence.

Judge Hixson also rejected Apple’s suggestion that a Special Master conduct the review, arguing that given the level of familiarity with the case required to assess the relevance of these documents, Epic was the only practical option for determining whether Apple had systematically misclassified them.

Realistically, the only person who has the practical ability to determine if Apple has been systematically mis-coding documents as nonresponsive is its opponent, Epic.

In his decision, the judge agreed with Apple that the company should be allowed to review the documents for privileged and sensitive information before producing them to Epic, and authorized Apple to designate all documents produced as part of the exercise as Attorneys’ Eyes Only.

Importantly, Judge Hixson has not yet determined whether Apple systematically misclassified responsive documents as nonresponsive, nor has he imposed the daily monetary sanctions originally requested by Epic.

Apple now has until December 8 to complete the document production, with Epic having until December 15 to file any objections, and Apple until December 22 to respond.

Industry observers note that coming from one of the biggest names in the cybersecurity space, Norton VPN is one of the most improved VPNs around. It now genuinely rivals the very best VPNs, and we even rate it as the best streaming VPN, ahead of the likes of NordVPN and Proton VPN.

It has been revealed that norton is celebrating the holiday season with some exciting Black Friday VPN deals. Its entry-level Standard plan is now $2.59 per month ($69.93 upfront) and runs for 27 months, including three extra months free.

It has been revealed that however, the real stars of the show are Norton VPN Plus and Ultimate. Plus has dropped to just $2.99 per month ($80.73 upfront) for 27 months, down from $3.49, while Ultimate is now $3.49 per month ($94.23 upfront) for 27 months, down from $4.49. These are the cheapest prices I’ve ever seen on Norton’s VPN suites.

Sources indicate that plus builds on Standard’s VPN and ad blocker with malware protection, AI-powered scam detection, a password manager, dark web monitoring, and 10 GB of cloud backup. Ultimate goes one step further, adding parental controls, 50 GB of cloud storage, and coverage for up to 20 devices, double what Standard and Plus allow.

Norton VPN Standard | 68% off | 2 years + 3 months FREENow: $2.59 per monthNorton VPN is more complete than ever. It’s fast and private, with an audited no-logs policy and a seriously effective ad blocker, and it unblocks everything. This limited-time Black Friday deal, particularly on the feature-packed Plus proposal, makes it an easy recommendation.

What you'll get:📱 Easy-to-use VPN apps📺 Powerful streaming unblocking⚡ Fast speeds🔒 Independently audited.

This two-year Norton VPN Standard blueprint costs $2.59 per month ($69.93 upfront for 27 months) and comes with an industry-leading 60-day money-back guarantee so you can test it out risk-free.

Norton VPN does a good job in pretty much every area that matters, but it’s hands down the best streaming VPN we’ve tested. In our latest tests, Norton VPN unblocked Netflix libraries in every location we tried, along with Disney+, Prime Video, BBC iPlayer, ITV, Channel 4, and TVNZ+. Its unblocking power beat significant hitters like NordVPN, Proton VPN, and Surfshark.

There are also apps for major screens, including Apple TV, Google TV, Android TV, and Amazon Fire TV. Admittedly, it isn't as fast as Proton VPN or ExpressVPN, two of the fastest VPNs we've tested. But at over 1,000 Mbps in our tests, it's more than fast enough for seamless, lag-free 4K streaming and anything else you need it for.

Recent findings suggest that privacy is in safe hands, too. Norton's strict no-logs policy was independently audited by VerSprite in 2025, and the tech giant publishes transparency reports four times a year. You also get a reliable kill switch, multi-hop connections, IP rotation, which swaps your IP address every few seconds in six countries, and Mimic, Norton's own stealth protocol, which disguises your VPN traffic so it's harder to block on restrictive networks.

Its Plus initiative, at $2.99 per month, packs a lot under one roof and is actually better value than Proton VPN’s $2.49 plan, which has no extras like these, or ExpressVPN Basic at $2.79 per month, which includes ad blockers and a private AI assistant but no password manager or cloud backup.

In a recent development, norton VPN isn't without its shortcomings, though. Its device limit counts installed devices rather than active connections, so once you hit the cap you'll need to remove a device before adding a new one. If you need unlimited simultaneous connections, go for Surfshark ($2.29 per month), or Private Internet Access ($1.49 a month) if you're on a tighter budget.

All in all, Norton VPN is excellent value for money, particularly if streaming is high on your list. Plus at $2.99 per month is the sweet spot, above all if you’re after an all-in-one internet security suite. You also get a 60-day money-back guarantee, which is double the industry standard, so you can try it risk-free.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Readdle updated its Documents app for iPhone and iPad this week with Voice Notes, a new AI-powered feature that lets owners record conversations and automatically generate transcripts, summaries, and follow-up notes. Here are the details.

While the habit of recording meetings, lectures, or even one’s own thoughts is not particularly new, modern AI tools and models have made it considerably easier to extract useful information from these recordings without having to listen back to them in their entirety or take copious notes that can distract from the actual conversation.

This week, Readdle’s Documents introduced Voice Notes, which “lets you record audio and turn it into a summary, follow-ups, and a full transcript,” as the firm put it.

Sources indicate that users can start a newly introduced recording session by tapping the “+” button in the app and selecting Voice Notes. Alternatively, they can start recording from the iPhone’s Action button, which is a nice touch.

Once they’re done, Readdle indicates Documents can generate:.

Users can cycle through these three tabs, where they can also listen to the original recording or copy and share the information.

Readdle says Voice Notes can recognize multiple languages in the same conversation, with the actual transcript preserving the languages as spoken, “while the summary and follow-ups are generated in the most frequently spoken language.”.

Sources indicate that each voice note is saved as a single file in Documents that contains the original recording, transcript, summary, and follow-ups. Users can organize these files into folders, share them, sync them with their cloud storage, and save the transcript as a separate .txt file.

However, if people give a voice note’s AI-generated content a thumbs down, Readdle may retain its transcript and summary for up to six months, or until the user objects to their processing, whichever comes first.

The organization also says user data isn’t used to train AI models, although third-party AI providers may retain inputs for up to 30 days for abuse and misuse monitoring, or longer if required by law.

Now, I'm one of those people who hates deleting their favorite games just to make space for a newly introduced one. I scratched my head, asking myself, "Do I delete Cyberpunk? Or do I delete Assassin's Creed Shadows?".

Recent findings suggest that and then, the solution came to me in the form of a glorious PS5 internal SSD. Enter the SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 850P, which has just dropped in price especially for Black Friday. In both the U.S. and the U.K., you can save on the plug-and-play SSD.

If you're based in the U.K. like I am, both the 1TB and 2TB versions of the internal SSD are discounted. You can get the 1TB version for just £222 at Amazon, and the 2TB version for £545.

Recent findings suggest that the SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 850P is available in four storage configurations: 1TB, 2TB, 4TB and 8TB. The 2TB version is at the moment discounted in the U.S., available for $569 directly from PlayStation, as is the 4TB version, which is down to $899 at Amazon U.S.

The 850P is officially licensed by PlayStation and comes in four configurations: 1TB, 2TB, 4TB and 8TB. I've been using the 2TB version and it offers more than enough space for small and large games alike. As its name suggests, the 850P is an internal SSD, and there's a dedicated slot for M.2 NVMe drivers under your PS5's hood, regardless of the model.

Industry observers note that what I love about the 850P is just how easy it is to use. This is a plug-and-play hard drive. To install it, you need to turn over your PS5 and pop out the top panel. You'll see a silver plate which you can unscrew using a small star screwdriver. Once that's done, you need to remove another screw (and its spacer), slot in your 850P, and put the screw and spacer back in.

Industry observers note that now all that's left to do is reinsert everything you took out and pop the PS5's panel back into place. Et voilà! You're good to go. Fire up your PS5 and you'll be prompted to format the 850P before using it. This takes under two minutes, and after that, you can start installing games.

You'll then be able to see the 850P appear as "M.2 SSD Storage" on the PS5's home screen — if you've got the storage widget active, of course. If not, you can dive into system settings to see if it's working a-okay (which it most certainly will be).

The 850P offers fast read and write speeds. You get sequential read speeds up to 7,300 MB/s, which means that game loading times are rapid. There's barely any waiting time! Write speeds up to 6,600 MB/s also mean that copying from disc to console is supremely fast. I couldn't believe how quickly I was able to install Detroit Become Human!

Lastly, the 850P features heatsink which ensures the SSD remains cool and doesn't overheat. There's so much to love about this nifty little device, and as a PS5 owner, it's saved me the headache of deleting games every time I buy a new one.

Industry observers note that right now, you can grab the 4TB model for just $899 at Amazon U.S., and the 2TB version for £406 at Amazon U.K. These Black Friday deals are too good to pass up on, and I recommend grabbing them as soon as you can!

Sources indicate that apple’s share of US smartphone shipments jumped from 50% to 57% year over year last quarter, with the firm being the only major smartphone maker to buck the broader trend of declining shipments. Here are the details.

In a recent development, yesterday, we covered a Counterpoint Research report on Q3 Latin American smartphone shipments, which highlighted Apple recording the smallest year-over-year decline among the region’s top five smartphone makers. As a result, Apple increased its share of regional shipments from 7% to 9%.

The report echoed the findings of several others published throughout this year, which showed how Apple has managed to navigate component shortages and rising costs better than many of its competitors, some of which have had to raise smartphone prices multiple times.

Apple, by contrast, kept iPhone pricing largely stable for much of the year, holding off on broader price increases until the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro lineup in September.

Today, Counterpoint Research released its report on US smartphone shipments for Q3, which indicated that Apple increased its share from 50% to 57% year over year, amid a 9% decline in overall shipments.

According to a separate Counterpoint report published last Thursday, Apple was the only major smartphone maker to avoid a year-over-year decline in shipment volume during the quarter.

In a recent development, in today’s report, Counterpoint notes that rising memory costs hit the low-end Android segment particularly hard during the quarter. Samsung was the only major Android smartphone maker to increase its shipment share, seeing a one-percentage-point bump to 25%, “helped by a portfolio spanning flagships and the low-end Galaxy A-series.”.

Carriers also felt the impact of the broader downturn, with smartphone sales across the three major US carriers collectively falling 4% year over year, per the report.

Looking ahead, Counterpoint expects memory costs to remain elevated and US carriers to be more selective with their holiday promotions, with smartphone sales expected to remain weak in Q4 despite it typically being the strongest quarter of the year.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • South Korea’s Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) announced today that it has opened formal proceedings against Apple over its advertising of Apple Intelligence features for the iPhone 16 lineup.
  • Back in March 2025, shortly after Apple declared it was delaying the rollout of what would eventually become Siri AI, the South Korean civic group Seoul YMCA filed a complaint with the KFTC.
  • At the time, Yonhap reported that the organization had previously called on Apple to compensate affected customers, and alleged that the organization may have continued to market the iPhone 16 lineup despite already knowing that some of its advertised AI features would be delayed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

South Korea’s Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) announced today that it has opened formal proceedings against Apple over its advertising of Apple Intelligence features for the iPhone 16 lineup. Here are the details.

Back in March 2025, shortly after Apple declared it was delaying the rollout of what would eventually become Siri AI, the South Korean civic group Seoul YMCA filed a complaint with the KFTC.

At the time, Yonhap reported that the organization had previously called on Apple to compensate affected customers, and alleged that the organization may have continued to market the iPhone 16 lineup despite already knowing that some of its advertised AI features would be delayed.

As 9to5Mac readers will likely remember, Apple widely advertised Apple Intelligence and AI-powered Siri features as part of its iPhone 16 launch campaign, going so far as to give its iconic Fifth Avenue store an Apple Intelligence-themed makeover and run an ad campaign starring Bella Ramsey.

It has been revealed that this landed Apple in legal and regulatory trouble in multiple markets, including the US, where the company agreed to a $250 million class action settlement earlier this year, and Brazil, where it came under scrutiny from a consumer protection agency in May. Now, the company is facing potential penalties in South Korea as well.

According to recent reports, as a result of Seoul YMCA’s complaint, the KFTC conducted an investigation into Apple’s advertising practices. Today, the regulator announced (via MacRumors) that its investigators had submitted their findings and recommendations for formal deliberation by the Commission.

According to the KFTC’s press release, investigators concluded that Apple advertised Apple Intelligence and its planned staggered rollout on the iPhone 16 website, but “concealed, downplayed, or omitted information material to consumers’ purchasing decisions.”.

That included, per the press release (translation ours):.

The press release also notes that Genmoji, Image Playground, “Siri with the ability to understand personal context,” and “Siri that provides step-by-step guidance” were not made available as advertised:.

For example, Siri’s ability to understand personal context was advertised as being scheduled to launch first in US English by the end of 2024, as currently available in US English in October 2024, and as scheduled to support Korean in early April 2025.

In reality, the feature was not rolled out in US English until September 2026, with Korean language support following in October 2026.

As a result, the investigators concluded that Apple’s conduct constituted a violation of the country’s Labeling and Advertising Act, which prohibits deceptive labeling and advertising.

They recommended issuing corrective orders, including a prohibition on such conduct in the future, as well as imposing a financial penalty.

They also estimate that Apple’s revenue associated with the alleged violation amounts to approximately 3.35 trillion South Korean won (roughly $2.5 billion), though the KFTC’s press release does not specify the amount of the fine.

⁠Yonhap noted today that the fine could reach roughly $48 million, while ⁠KBS reported that it could range between $21 million and $42 million.

With the report now submitted, Apple has six weeks to submit its written defense before the Commission deliberates and makes a final determination on whether the organization violated the law and, if so, how much it should be fined.

Revision, November 27, 12:08 p.m. ET: In a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple mentioned:.

Recent findings suggest that at Apple, we deeply value the relationship with our customers in Korea and have always focused on delivering the best products and services in the world. Since we added Korean language support for Apple Intelligence last year, people have benefited from dozens of powerful features that are integrated across Apple’s platforms. And we have continued to build on that commitment with the recent launch of Korean language support for Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri that’s more capable, conversational, and personal. We have cooperated with the KFTC’s investigation and disagree with the conclusions in the Examiner’s Report. We look forward to presenting a fulsome defense before the Commission.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Open the page and your phone is a node. The scheduler sends it a pod, and the pod's program runs on a Linux kernel booted in the tab. Close the tab and the node is gone, and Kubernetes starts the pod on someone else's.

Scan to become a node, or use the browser you are reading this in.

Joining downloads about 5 MB and runs a small Linux guest in the tab, on one core, until you close the tab.

The control plane in the middle, a node for each tab, and each Service on the way to the pods behind it. A node is filled when its pod is running. An orange dot is a request you sent, on its way to the pod that answered, and a green one is a tile of the picture on its way to the node that rendered it.

In a recent development, how long a tab takes to start its pod: from the tab being handed the pod to the pod's program running, which is the page loading, the kernel booting and the image being mounted. The last 0 starts.

According to recent reports, how long the cluster takes to answer: from the agent handing a request to the Service to the answer being back from a pod in someone's tab, timed on the cluster's machine. The last 0 requests, from every visitor, by the milliseconds each took.

No request has been answered yet.

Send a request to a Service. One of the pods behind it answers, on whoever's phone that is, and counts the visit in a Redis on someone else's.

Recent findings suggest that press the button and the cluster draws a Mandelbrot set. The picture is split into 64 tiles, and each node's pod computes its share in awk, on the Linux in its tab. Point at a tile to see which device drew it.

One picture at a time, for everyone.

The cluster's Services that have a pod on a tab behind them, read from the API server.

In a recent development, nothing yet. A tab that joins reveals up here.

What the nodes are, by what their browsers say.

No tab is a node right now. Yours can be the first.

Recent findings suggest that the control plane is an ordinary Kubernetes, and a pod is an ordinary pod. The marked line is the only one that is upcoming: the scheduler puts a pod that has it on a tab, and every other pod on the cluster's own machine.

Build your own amp modeler: $78 DIY pedal kit from TONE3000

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (686 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Guitarworld

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • TONE3000 has sought to bring the biggest disruptor of today’s amp modeling game to the masses in a novel way by partnering with Daisy Audio for a DIY pedal kit.
  • This isn’t your standard build-it-yourself overdrive or fuzz pedal.
  • Sources indicate that it’s an enticing prospect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

TONE3000 has sought to bring the biggest disruptor of today’s amp modeling game to the masses in a novel way by partnering with Daisy Audio for a DIY pedal kit.

This isn’t your standard build-it-yourself overdrive or fuzz pedal. Instead, this is a fully fledged capture and IR player that can be completely assembled at home, and tap into the ever-growing network of Neural Amp Modeler (NAM) tones.

Sources indicate that it’s an enticing prospect. TONE3000 and the free-to-use NAM A2 have taken the gear world by storm this year, rewriting the rules of amp modeling in the process.

NAM A2 is widely believed to be one of the best modeling technologies of today, outperforming the industry’s massive guns in a blind listening test. What’s more, it’s an open-source platform that lets players create, download and use captures of amps and effects for free.

Blackstar, Fractal, HeadRush, Positive Grid, Line 6 and Fender are all cottoning on to the game-changing tech – TONE3000 even launched a free plugin to play captures – but now NAM A2 hype has reached fever pitch with this latest partnership.

According to TONE3000, every part of the pedal is open source, from the firmware and companion app to the schematic, circuit board, and drill template. In other words, anyone can build the pedal.

And it looks like a neat pedal, too. Once assembled, it has room for four presets, with a rotary switch to go between them. There’s a three-band EQ, as well as controls for Input, Output, and Noise Gate.

All the latest guitar news, interviews, lessons, reviews, deals and more, direct to your inbox!

Recent findings suggest that once together, it can host any NAM A2 capture, of which there are quite literally hundreds of thousands. It can also stack captures, too, or run primary models into an Impulse Response.

Of course, this is way more advanced than wiring up an overdrive pedal, so the build is not for the faint of heart. TONE3000 goes as far as to suggest you should have at least two home builds under your belt before even thinking about this one.

According to recent reports, it has about 150 solder joints, plus 14 wires to jacks, footswitch, and the rotary control. It has a through-hole construction, with no surface-mount parts. It’s all built on the Daisy Audio Seed3 module, which costs just $34.99.

The rest of the hardware comes separately courtesy of Tayda Electronics. That set is priced at $42.99, and comes with the circuit board, aluminum enclosure, and all the remaining bells and whistles. In all, that amounts to $77.98 for the entire pedal kit.

For those who aren’t afraid, the chassis has been made plenty major enough to inject a few modifications of your own.

“Daisy was built so anyone could turn an idea into a real piece of audio hardware,” claims Daisy co-founder, Andrew Ikenberry.

Recent findings suggest that “TONE3000 has taken state-of-the-art neural modeling and open-sourced every piece of the pedal around it, which is exactly the kind of project we hoped Daisy would make possible. We can't wait to see what builders do with it.”.

Head over to TONE3000 to find out more and read the Build Guide, and visit Daisy Audio and Tayda Electronics for the parts needed.

When he’s not combining his passion for writing and music during his day job, Matt performs with indie rock duo Esme Emerson, and has previously opened for the likes of Ed Sheeran, Keane, Japanese House and Good Neighbours.
