#166906. The Balatro Timeline

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 28m • 📚 Deep Dive (5534 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Localthunk ↗ Open Full Page

The Balatro Timeline

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 28 min read (5534 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Localthunk

⏱️ ~28 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, it’s been approximately 3 years since I began work on Balatro - and in that time I have personally documented almost nothing about the journey.
  • This is the creation date for template, a folder in my Learning/Lua/ directory.
  • I had saved up about 3 weeks of vacation time from my IT job, and since they didn’t allow people to accrue vacation year over year I just took off a bunch of time in December to work on some kind of project.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it’s been approximately 3 years since I began work on Balatro - and in that time I have personally documented almost nothing about the journey. This is something that has bothered me since the game debuted. I am constantly forgetting major moments in development or milestones. It’s about time I start writing down what happened, I say better late than never!This is an account of everything related to Balatro development in chronological order, up to and including the launch day. This should tell the story but more importantly it will serve as a source of truth for me when I look back on this time in a few years to recall the details correctly. I already notice talking to friends, players, and media that I contradict myself on some of the details from time to time. I’ll try and keep this up to date as I remember more about what happened.

This is the creation date for template, a folder in my Learning/Lua/ directory. This is the creation of the project that would eventually become Balatro.

I had saved up about 3 weeks of vacation time from my IT job, and since they didn’t allow people to accrue vacation year over year I just took off a bunch of time in December to work on some kind of project. At the very beginning of this time off I was working on a game called Autohike. I had been working on this game for a few months at this point but I wasn’t really feeling it anymore, so very early into my vacation I pivoted to cleaning up the code I had created and making a template for a latest game.

The initial idea on Dec 13th was to create an online multiplayer version of Big Cheat, a game that a few friends and I had invented many years prior and played a ton based on the card games Big 2 and Cheat.

This whole first week was mostly me trying to upgrade the engine I built with Autohike to better fit a card game.

This is the creation date for CardGame, my current production working folder for all Balatro source code. I never bothered changing the name.

I remember spending a long time making custom pixel art for the red deck back and all the playing cards. It was the first time I had tried making proper pixel art.

I had a very weird prototype. There were no Jokers, there were no blinds to select, the upgrade system consisted of randomly choosing a card from the deck and slapping a weird ‘enhancement’ on it. But it definitely had the bones of Balatro at this point, so it was pretty clear that I abandoned the online Substantial Cheat idea immediately.

It has been revealed that the game had the CHIP X MULT mechanic already. I really don’t know where this idea came from but it seemed very natural for a scoring system. Earlier in December I was watching videos of Luck Be a Landlord from Northernlion and that whole score attack concept really fuelled the direction I wanted to go with this game from this point onward.

I also made a very conscious effort not to play any more roguelike games starting now. I want to be crystal clear here and say that this was not because I thought it would result in a better game, this was because making games is my hobby, releasing them and making money from them is not, so naively exploring roguelike design (and especially deckbuilder design, since I had never played one before) was part of the fun for me. I wanted to make mistakes, I wanted to reinvent the wheel, I didn’t want to borrow tried-and-true designs from existing games. That likely would have resulted in a more tight game but it would have defeated the purpose of what I love about making games.

I started sharing progress with a few of my friends, but no builds were shared yet.

In a recent development, my vacation is over, but I am now fully immersed and obsessed. This is my favourite feeling in the world. When I was back in University I would routinely stay up until the wee hours of the morning working on my weird game projects and greet my parents while they made their morning coffee. I got back into this groove and starting in January I was hooked.

Evenings and weekends were Joker Poker time (my working title for Balatro, likely decided on early this month).

I iterate through some weird versions of the game, including a version where the only way to upgrade anything is to upgrade the cards in your deck in a sort of pseudo-shop, and those cards can be upgraded multiple times (think like Super Auto Pets, pets have different XP/levels when combined, same idea).

I started adding Jokers to the game. I also was temporarily working remotely out of province for a few months starting at this time and found that my Balatro dev time took a pretty massive hit.

I started adding different boss blinds to the game.

Early March marked an vital event in the history of Balatro, and I wanted to describe why things happened the way they did. I stopped working on the project entirely.

I have been making games for about 10 years now and I have been doing visual art projects for much longer, and a very important habit I have developed for creative hobby projects is to stop working on something when I no longer feel the drive. This is for 2 main reasons; first, it allows me to move on to the next idea without totally burning out on the last thing. Second, and more importantly in this case, it allows me to take time off guilt free and possibly come back to the project later on without wrapping it in negative emotions.

In a recent development, we are so back. This is the last month I am away from home but I start carving out my evenings and weekends to work on Joker Poker again.

My brain is teeming with ideas, I’m so excited about the game again, and I have a ton of momentum.

I create (and quickly scrap) a bunch of new systems to test, such as a separate currency for rerolls outside of $, and a ‘golden seal’ to be added to playing cards when you skip all blinds that returns that card to hand after it has been played.

It is during this burst of productivity that I first start thinking about a possible Steam release of the game. This was the first time in my then 8 years of game development that I had even considered publicly releasing a game I had made. Normally they just end up going to a couple of friends, but honestly the main purpose of my games wasn’t for them to be consumed, but rather for them just to be made.

Another factor me starting to consider a Steam launch was that my partner was almost finished her PhD and the writing was on the wall that we may be moving out of province for good as she looked for a job. If this was the case, I would have to quit my job and look for work. I thought why not try and get a game developer job somewhere? To accomplish that, I thought having a Steam game in my portfolio would be a massive benefit.

I really didn’t have any commercial aspirations at this time. All I knew about Steam is that there were about a million games on there and that very few could realistically make a living, so I didn’t think it was possible to consider it.

It was in during this month that my eventual developer name - LocalThunk - was incepted.

According to recent reports, my partner was learning to code in R at the time, and she asked me “How do you name your variables?” I went on some rant about casing, using descriptive words, underscores, etc. She waits until I am finished and notes “I like to call mine thunk”. I thought that was just about the funniest thing I had ever heard.

Industry observers note that the way variables are declared in Lua is (sometimes) with the local keyword, thus local thunk was born! I wouldn’t choose this name for quite a while yet but this is the moment I looked back on when I was finally ready to create a developer handle online.

In a recent development, still working on the game (details of what exactly I was adding at this point are fuzzy). I think by this time Joker Poker has economy, a bunch of Jokers, and generally resembles the current version of Balatro.

I share a fresh version of the game with some friends.

Sources indicate that one of those friends gets back to me months later with very high praise. Unexpectedly high. He mentions that he has played the beta for dozens of hours.

In all my years of sharing projects with friends I had never received feedback like that. I couldn’t believe it, and it really pushed me over the edge to fully flesh out this idea. It was really great knowing that this game was actually being enjoyed by someone I know, and I wanted to prove to him, my other friends, my partner, my family, and myself that I could make something really fun and interesting.

At this point I started really increasing scope. More Jokers, Controller support, touch support, Jimbo the cheeky tutorial character, a soundtrack, proper sound effects, special editions for cards, and way more got added to the docket. I felt like scope creep incarnate, and it was amazing.

Industry observers note that as anticipated, my partner got a really great job in a different province and I quit my job to move there with her. I was really excited for this latest chapter in our lives, and I also decided to not look for work for the next 3-6 months and develop Joker Poker full time.

It was the perfect opportunity to work as a game dev full time (even if for free) and I didn’t know if I would ever have the chance again. I had some money saved up, so starting this month I really leaned into it.

I took a brief vacation to surf in California with some friends. I highlighted them the new build I had been working on - a version that would end up on Steam within a few months. This version now had Vouchers!

Recent findings suggest that this month I contacted Luis Clemente on the freelance website Fiverr and he delivered an absolutely amazing soundtrack for Joker Poker. Really knocked it out of the park. I was very nervous about this because it was (at the time) the only money I had spent or planned to spend on the game.

Recent findings suggest that I also revealed the game to some friends during a discord call, and one friend made the suggestion that there should be a flaming effect on your score if you get a really good hand. I hated the idea at first, but I sat with it for a while and knew I was wrong. That flaming score effect really fit perfectly with the game I was trying to create. Sure glad I listened to him!

I workshopped a list of ~20 names for the game. I saw that the game ‘Joker Poker’ was already an app on the app store, but beyond that it felt just a bit too silly for the vibe I was shooting for. I sent this list of new names to my friends and got all of their feedback. Balatro was among that list but nobody picked it. Something about it really stuck with me so I just went with it.

I started creating store assets this month. I created a trailer, got my screenshots, and paid the very scary $100 Steam fee to upload a game. I also had a pretty massive code refactor at this point.

The name is officially Balatro.

Industry observers note that I was pretty overwhelmed by Steam, just starting to look into things like how to launch an indie game? was really freaking me out. There are so many games released on Steam every day and so much noise about what you should and shouldn’t do, what type of game you should make, what method you should use to market it. It was a real shock to me that even though I had this game that I poured so much time into that it didn’t really seem to matter. I didn’t think this game would sell any copies before this and my initial research into Steam reinforced that idea to me.

According to recent reports, I downloaded Slay the Spire and played it for the first time. Holy shit. now that is a game.

I did this because I was having some troubles in my controller implementation and I wanted to see how they handled controller inputs for a card game but I ended up getting sucked in. Thank goodness I avoided playing it until now because I surely would have just copied their incredible design (intentionally or subconsciously).

In late May, I uploaded the first public Beta build to Steam, set my store page live, and saw exactly what I expected to happen happened: nothing. The fact that I wasn’t anticipating any fanfare probably saved me some heartache because I didn’t end up feeling dejected from the very tepid response my free Beta was getting from players.

It has been revealed that feedback started coming in from the Beta players. This marks the beginning of a more player-focused development strategy I would adhere to instead of just listening to my gut all the time.

By end of May, Balatro had 48 wishlists on Steam.

This is about the time when Balatro stopped being a pure hobby for me.

In a recent development, youTubers started covering the game. It was mostly small and indie game specific channels, but the attention definitely started growing over time. The Discord server I had made for feedback about the game started taking up more of my time. However, at this time there was nothing to indicate that the game was going to start popping off.

Even so - I started really thinking about the commercial viability of the game. Could I actually make some money from this? I saw a glimmer of a possibility that this might turn into something.

It has been revealed that my partner and I went on a major backcountry canoe trip for a few days. During this trip we talked about the future of this game and what it meant for my work. Even with the mild momentum I was ready to move on, and since back in January I told her this would be at most 6 months I felt that I shouldn’t push it too much longer. It had already been a year and a half of dev at this point.

It has been revealed that I prepared to launch the game in 2 weeks. The release date went live on my Steam page, and I started thinking about moving on to looking for a job again and getting back into normal software/IT work.

In a recent development, I got a DM on twitter from a scout at Playstack, my eventual publisher. I was super excited but this also complicated things. This was a very tumultuous time in the history of the game because I was in limbo between nothing will come of this game and I want to move on with my life and what if I could do this as a job?

By June 10th, Balatro had 183 wishlists on Steam.

Dan Gheesling plays Balatro on his stream. This is a massive streamer for my game (and a great guy!), and it starts making my wishlist numbers spike.

Other medium sized Youtubers and streamers start playing the game, it is building momentum. At this point the game was spreading entirely from word of mouth. I had posted a few things on Reddit and Twitter but really nothing that ever gained meaningful traction; now the game had inertia by itself.

In a recent development, it becomes clear that I should pursue the game a little further. I am approached by a few different publishers around now. I get some really great support and advice from my parents about everything going on. I strongly consider going it alone, but I also know that I need some help with all the public facing things, marketing, possible porting and just navigating this newly introduced thing I knew nothing about.

I hire a lawyer to help me with all the contract negotiations, help me set up a business, and I decide to sign with Playstack after speaking to studios that have worked with them in the past. They can replace whatever salary I would have made from an IT job, so this is my job now!

While this was a very exciting time, it was also incredibly stressful. I’m not used to dealing with so many people, and I felt pressure from so many different directions that I wasn’t expecting.

In a recent development, I created a demo version of the game that only lasted 50 rounds after my free Beta tester queue started getting bigger. At this point I had 300 beta testers for the full game and didn’t really need any more. This demo strategy wasn’t the best idea, but it allowed people to see what Balatro was all about without just getting the full game for free. The demo was getting around 10-20 concurrent players, which was really mind blowing for me at the time.

By end of June, Balatro had 2440 wishlists on Steam.

I release big updates around this time for the playtesters. I add the skip tag system, and I totally revamp the tutorial to basically what it is today.

Sources indicate that the trajectory for the game appears at this time to be massive enough for me to replace my income for a year at least. This was so exciting to me, I hadn’t really thought about it before because I was doing this work on my weekends and during my evenings anyway.

Sources indicate that after a bunch of negotiations I finally sign a publishing deal with Playstack. I won’t go too far into whether or not people should or shouldn’t have a publisher, but for me at this time it was crucial that I have some publishing help. They outlined a very sensible release plan for the game (one that we adhered to almost exactly until launch in Feb 2024) and they really expanded the audience a ton with support for more languages and porting on day 1 for every major console.

Sources indicate that my demo is getting some attention from streamers still, but one day in mid July, Northernlion was pitched the game on his stream from Dan Gheesling and ended up playing it that same day. I was in the chat watching, totally dumbfounded, that someone I watched on Twitch/YouTube for over a decade at that point was playing my game. I text all my friends about it, they are all shocked as well. At the time I was more concerned about a potential crash or something going horribly wrong but I did also try to just sit, watch, and enjoy the surreal moment.

Recent findings suggest that northernlion was playing the 50 round demo version - and after he quickly ran through all 50 rounds I got his attention and gave him a key to play the full beta version. I think some people weren’t super fond of this because he got special treatment - but honestly I was more in fan mode than dev mode. Looking back I’m glad I gave him the key - that was a massive moment for my game and even though it was tricky to navigate.

Playstack and I decide that we should take down the demo and come up with a better strategy than limiting players to 50 rounds.

By end of July, Balatro had 28,661 wishlists on Steam.

The latest demo strategy is in place, and most of August is me preparing for a September release of this demo. The plan now is to make the demo content limited instead of round limited. This means that players can play as much as they want, which is much more sensible.

The demo should be ready a couple weeks before the Fall 2023 Next Fest in October. Next Fest is a festival set up by Steam to shine a spotlight on upcoming games for the platform. While we weren’t planning on adding Balatro as an official entry in the October 2023 Next Fest - we thought having a demo available at the same time as the festival might gather some incidental attention.

Sources indicate that this is when my sleep and heart started having challenges. I have talked about this a tiny bit in the past, but I really struggled with my physical and mental health from this time onward all the way up to launch. This was entirely because of the stress around dealing with the public, players, and the pressure to get everything done before February 2024.

It has been revealed that we start exploring the feasibility of porting the game to different platforms. I won’t talk about this much more because of the agreements around those platforms, but suffice it to say this ended up being a very large portion of my work time over the coming months.

By end of August, Balatro had 38,011 wishlists on Steam.

I start converting all the text in the game to an external english file to facilitate localization to other languages. I didn’t blueprint on having this game translated when it was a hobby so I had to do this all after the fact. It didn’t end up being too horrible, just some rework that I could have saved if I knew I was doing this from the beginning.

Industry observers note that near the end of September, I launch the new demo on Steam. People generally really like it! I try and make some tweaks based on player feedback, but it’s clear this approach is much better than limiting players to 50 rounds.

The last few months I have been very involved in the Balatro Discord server. I try and chat with players all the time, and I try to take their criticisms seriously. I feel like the demo and beta players knew more about how to play the game properly than I did, so I found it was really notable to listen to what they had to say about the game in order to properly assess what I need to change or tweak for balance.

By the time the September demo is live, there are tons of players chatting in the Discord server all the time. I feel pretty overwhelmed by it all but I feel like I need to interact with them constantly. I didn’t want to waste the opportunity, and we also chatted a lot about general design things that players might be interested to see in the full 1.0 version of the game.

By end of September, Balatro had 49,791 wishlists on Steam.

Next Fest goes live early in the month, and as anticipated we do catch a lot of attention for having a demo live at the same time. We get pretty good coverage in general around this time from YouTubers, streamers, and even some media.

We originally planned on taking the demo down a week or so after the Next Fest ended, but so many people kept playing it that we decided to keep that version of the demo live for quite a while longer.

I started finalizing the content plan for the 1.0 version of the game. The biggest addition is the inclusion of a sort of ‘ascension’ system. This is from Slay the Spire (see? Told you I’d steal from it) but I think it was a super cool way to add difficulty and give players a sort of checklist to work through.

In a recent development, I also had a meeting with Playstack this month where I described to them the final content in the game, including ‘120 Jokers’. Later that week I had another meeting with them, and someone mentioned something about 150 Jokers. I couldn’t remember if I accidentally mentioned I was going to make 150 or if they misheard me, but either way I thought that 150 was a much better number so I added 30 more Jokers to the plan.

Sources indicate that I can’t remember if it was now or in September, but we enlist the help of Maarten De Meyer to help with our porting efforts. Maarten was absolutely instrumental in getting Balatro on every platform, and frankly he’s a Love2D wizard.

My sleep and my heart are getting worse. Every few nights I need to sleep sitting upright on the couch because sleeping while lying down kept getting interrupted by my heart. I stupidly thought that I couldn’t handle going to the doctor while dealing with all the dev and business stuff swirling around at the time. I felt totally overwhelmed.

By end of October, Balatro had 77,380 wishlists on Steam.

Recent findings suggest that we keep the demo up for the entire month of November since our player numbers are still pretty high. More of the same from previous months. This is basically crunch time, so for the next couple months I’m just working on finishing everything in my plan.

The game is to be released right after the following Next Fest scheduled for February 2024. This means that we want a new version of the demo with slightly different content to be available for that Next Fest, so I am working on that on the side.

Additionally, we have an idea to make an invitational tournament for streamers with an early build of this new version of the demo. This is scheduled to happen some time in late January 2024.

By end of November, Balatro had 87,280 wishlists on Steam.

Sources indicate that more of the same. By this time it’s clear we can launch on every platform thanks to monumental effort by both Maarten and his wizardry and also a massive amount of optimization to my code base that I had worked on over the previous months.

We decide to take down the demo by the end of December because we want some breathing room before we launch the next iteration.

By end of December, Balatro had 94,212 wishlists on Steam.

My heart is really bothering me. I routinely can’t sleep until the sun comes up, and my mental health is really suffering. I love working on the game but working on it so publicly and with such an intensity for so long is really catching up with me.

One night I am watching the movie The Abyss with my partner and suddenly I get tunnel vision, my heart is absolutely pounding and I feel like something is seriously wrong. I sit on the couch for a while, totally freaked out. I’m really scared.

I call my doctor and see him the next morning for an appointment. He assures me that this wasn’t a heart attack or heart failure but an anxiety attack. I am not normally an anxious person and have never had issues with this in the past but I think the intense stress for such a long time has done quite a bit of damage.

He asks me if my work has been stressful lately. I don’t even know how to explain.

January 19th is the invitational tournament. We have 6 streamers participate. This was actually a really great moment for me to sit back and watch the fruits of my labour for once - not work on the game and just enjoy.

My partner and I order sushi, sit down and watch the multi-stream broadcast by MurphyObv playing a hilarious character. It was probably my favourite moment of the entire pre-launch phase of the game. Just really wonderful to see this silly game come together for a moment and watch a bunch of people participate like a community.

Hafu wins, because of course she does. She’s Hafu!

We announce the launch date of the game; February 20th.

By end of January, Balatro had 114,977 wishlists on Steam.

Sources indicate that I was still working on implementing stuff in the game in February believe it or not. I was in super crunch mode.

I had a private server made a little while earlier with testers from the Balatro community that I felt exhibited an exceptional ability to give feedback, understand the vision of the game, and analyze the flaws with it. I think this was instrumental in making sure that the 1.0 version of the game really started fun out the gate. I chatted with them a ton this month.

I knew there would be tweaks after launch but this was important to ensure that something catastrophic didn’t happen.

We have a really strong Next Fest. We get a ton of coverage from streamers, YouTubers, and media yet again. Balatro is one of the most played games of the festival.

According to recent reports, I start properly playing the game myself about a week before launch - and it’s actually fun. I have a pretty emotional moment where I feel like I did the thing I set out to do. Finally. I made the fun game I wanted to make.

We have an absurd amount of momentum leading up to launch day, far more than what anyone was expecting.

Sources indicate that february 19th rolls around. The 19th is the review embargo day, and Playstack did a truly exceptional job getting this game in the hands of traditional media to write their reviews before launch. I didn’t know what to expect, this was a pretty weird game after all. Average ratings of 6 or 7?

The first substantial review is from PC Gamer: 91. Playstack and I are on a call when they break the news to me, and I can tell they are pretty shocked. I am shocked. That rating doesn’t make any sense.

More ratings pour in, and by the time the day is done we are sitting above 90 on both Metacritic and OpenCritic. I wasn’t even thinking that this was a possibility, but it sure did build a ton of hype for launch day. I don’t think I would have rated Balatro higher than an 8 and I made the damn thing.

By launch day, Balatro has 208,401 wishlists on Steam.

In a recent development, february 20th, 8am PST is when the game is supposed to go live across all platforms. We launch it 15 minutes early. I cannot describe to you how nervous I am that I’ll be patching like a madman not only all day, but all month. I told my partner that I won’t be making any prepares until the end of March because I fully anticipated the sky to fall and for me to be working 24/7 to fix the inevitable disaster.

It has been revealed that to my shock - nothing goes wrong. People love the game, they’re having a great time. I think there may have been some small bugs but definitely nothing massive, nothing like what I was anticipating. Streamers are playing it, media is writing about it. I have so many texts from friends and family. It is the most surreal day of my life.

The launch is 10-20 times larger than we were anticipating.

Recent findings suggest that one of the moments that sticks out to me is the moment I first checked the Steam page for sales. I checked this page for the first time a couple hours after launch almost on a whim, not expecting to see any sales information yet, and we had already sold 50,000 copies on Steam. The numbers on that page made no sense. This was meant for just a few of my friends and yet somehow all these strangers chose to buy it. The revenue on that page after just a couple hours was over $600,000, far more money than I’ve made in my entire life. By the end of launch day, Balatro has sold 119,000 units on Steam alone.

The other moment from that day that sticks out is later that day when my partner got home from work. She had been following along all day and struggling to get any work done, and when she got home she gave me a great big hug. I wasn’t sure I’d even survive the launch but here we were. I could not have done this without her. We ordered burgers for supper and popped a bottle of champagne to celebrate.

Breaking: Berkshire breaks out to record high with fourth-quarter rally reaching 19%

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1108 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.
  • Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.
  • The much more widely held B shares closed at latest highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.

Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.

The much more widely held B shares closed at latest highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.

The gains are in sharp contrast to the S&P 500's 1.2% dip as investors appear to be seeing Berkshire as a relatively safe haven amid worries about AI stocks and spending.

Both Berkshire classes were up 3.9% on the week as the S&P advanced by 2.5%, its best week since early August.

Berkshire's B shares are now 7.5 percentage points ahead of the benchmark for the year so far.

After erasing their post-Buffett CEO announcement losses three weeks ago, Berkshire shares are now up almost 10% since last year's shareholders meeting.

They've gained around 29% since last August's lows and are up around 18% year-to-date.

Berkshire Hathaway is due to disclose its quarterly equity portfolio snapshot on Monday when it files its Q3 13F with the SEC.

We won't know for sure until then, but numbers in the firm's third quarter 10-Q, released last Saturday, indicate Berkshire continued to reduce its Bank of America stake.

It would be the ninth consecutive quarter of selling.

As of June 30, Berkshire reported holding 483.4 million BAC shares valued now at $24.7 billion, it's fifth largest equity position.

On June 30, 2024, before the selling began, Berkshire owned just over 1 billion shares valued at $41.1 billion.

Since then, the number of shares in the portfolio has decreased by 53.2%, not including any Q3 sales, while the stock price has increased by 28.3%.

If there had been no reductions, the position would be worth $52.7 billion.

The belief Berkshire sold more BAC shares in the third quarter is based on a $372 million reduction in the cost basis for equities categorized by the organization as "banks, insurance, and finance.".

The 10-Q also reports $2.2 billion of pretax gains from equity sales.

Sources indicate that barron's notes Bank of America and American Express are the only financial stocks in the portfolio that have a cost basis low enough to generate a gain like that. Amex is one of the four stocks fresh CEO Greg Abel indicated would be held for "decades" to come in his February letter to shareholders.

In any case, Berkshire's almost 23% stake in Amex would have required it to quickly disclose any sales.

Based on the numbers in the 10-Q, the warrants Berkshire received as part of a 2011 $5 billion investment in the bank that it used in 2017 to buy 700 million shares at $7.14 each, and BAC's average stock price in the quarter, Barron's estimates 30 to 40 million shares may have been sold.

That would be roughly in line with the 30.2 million shares sold in the second quarter.

Recent findings suggest that the case isn't as good, but Barron's thinks Berkshire may have bought more Alphabet shares in the period. That's based on a $2.3 billion increase in the cost basis for the category that includes Google's parent.

Overall, it looks like it will be a relatively quiet quarter with $2.4 billion in equity purchases and $2.8 billion in sales.

Recent findings suggest that in the first quarter, Berkshire bought $15.9 billion and sold $24.1 billion of equities. In the second quarter, it purchased $23.5 billion and sold $3.7 billion.

All those numbers exclude the company's buybacks of its own stock.

In a term sheet filed early Friday, Berkshire Hathaway indicates it is selling more than 182 billion yen ($1.1 billion) worth of bonds with maturities between 2029 and 2056 and annual interest rates between 2.6% and 4.6%.

Bloomberg points out the rates, compared to benchmarks, are higher than its previous sale this year.

It quotes a fund manager as saying market sentiment "has become more sensitive," forcing issuers to make their offerings more attractive.

In April, Berkshire sold 272 billion yen ($1.7 billion) of bonds.

Berkshire uses the proceeds from the yen-denominated bonds to protect its ongoing investments in Japanese stocks from currency fluctuations.

Some links may require a subscription:.

Warren Buffett recommends Benjamin Graham's book, "The Intelligent Investor," and outlines what he considers Graham's three most key ideas.

WARREN BUFFETT: On investment books, if you're asking about that, I would recommend the first two books that Phil Fisher wrote back around 1960, "Common Sense [Stocks] and Uncommon Profits" and the second one ["Paths to Wealth Through Common Stocks"]. They're very good books.

You know, I obviously recommend, first and foremost, [Benjamin Graham's] "The Intelligent Investor," with chapters eight and 20 are the ones that you really should read.

Two of the — well, all of the vital ideas in investing, really, are in that book, because there's only about three ideas. And those — two of them are emphasized in those two chapters...

One is that — to think of yourself — to think of investing as owning a business and not buying something that wiggles around in price.

In a recent development, and the second one is your attitude, which ties in with that, the attitude toward the market, that's covered in chapter eight. And if you have the proper attitude toward market movements, it's an enormous help in securities.

And the final chapter is on the margin of safety, which means, don't try and drive a 9,800-pound truck over a bridge that states it's, you know, "Capacity: 10,000 pounds." But go down the road a little bit and find one that says, "Capacity: 15,000 pounds.".

Berkshire market capitalization: $1,259,897,054,755.

Berkshire Cash as of Sept 30: $377.4 billion (Up 3.3% from June 30).

Excluding Rail Cash and Subtracting T-Bills Payable: $352.3 billion (Down 1.9% from June 30).

Berkshire repurchased $9.6 billion of its shares in Q3 2026.

We dug through the full list of everything coming to Netflix in November 2026 to pull out three gems worth your long weekend: a nightmarish anime set in a sunless world where people turn into plants to survive, a gripping true-crime docuseries on one of the most divisive murder trials in recent memory, and Netflix's first Nordic medical drama, shot inside a real former emergency room.

According to recent reports, whatever you're in the mood for this holiday weekend, these three shows earn a spot on your watch list. Enjoy the family time (if you're celebrating right now) and buy yourself something shiny for Black Friday.

Industry observers note that true crime obsessives, this one's ready and waiting for you. "The Trials of Karen Read" revisits one of the most divisive murder cases in recent memory: the death of Boston police officer John O'Keefe, found in the snow outside a Canton, Massachusetts home in January 2022. It also extends to the two trials that followed for his girlfriend, Karen Read, and her status as a potential suspect. The first ended in a mistrial in 2024, and the second, in 2025, ended in her acquittal.

In a recent development, across three episodes, directors Danielle Johnson and Rob Miller follow the case from the initial investigation to the media spectacle it became, with the defense's claim that Read was framed in a police cover-up running underneath it all. It also includes interviews with jurors and with members of O'Keefe's own family. It's a twisty journey that's well worth investing in.

Watch "The Trials of Karen Read" on Netflix now.

Recent findings suggest that if you're after an anime that's got a new and inventive (as well as disturbing) hook, here it is. "Fool Night" takes place a century into a sunless future, where thick cloud cover has choked out the light. Humanity survives by "transplanting" people into Spirit Flowers, plants that generate the oxygen everyone else breathes. A young man named Toshiro Kamiya chooses to undergo the procedure, and the result is just as bleak and strange as that sounds.

This series marks the first team-up between Sunrise (the "Gundam" studio) and Shaft (of "Puella Magi Madoka Magica"), directed by Atsushi Yukawa of "Space Dandy" and adapted from Kasumi Yasuda's manga. And it promises to be a great-looking journey that you won't forget.

Watch "Fool Night" on Netflix on Nov. 26.

If you've burned through every season of your favorite hospital show, here's a latest one you haven't seen yet. "Always on Call" (original title "Legevakta") is Netflix Nordics' first-ever medical drama, a seven-episode Norwegian series set in a chaotic emergency room and filmed inside Oslo's real former ER.

Sara Khorami is Sofia, a surgeon juggling life-or-death cases, hospital politics, and the sordid personal lives of her colleagues. Created and written by Harald Rosenløw-Eeg and Jan Trygve Røyneland and directed by Stian Kristiansen and Liv Karin Dahlstrøm, it's a tight drama that you'll love getting to know with the rest of the world getting a glimpse of it for the first time.

Watch "Always on Call" on Netflix on Nov. 26.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The statement comes as Ukraine's allies sound the alarm over Russia's growing threat to European security and just one week after Trump's historic trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Asia.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

U.S. President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte issued a joint statement on Thursday urging Russia not to take any actions, intentionally or otherwise, that would further expand the Ukraine war.

The statement comes as Ukraine's allies sound the alarm over Russia's growing threat to European security and just one week after Trump's historic trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Asia.

Trump and Rutte described their meeting at the Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida on Wednesday as "very impactful," with Russia's nearly five-year-long war in Ukraine and the Iran war among the key topics of conversation.

"We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible," Trump and Rutte stated in their statement.

In a recent development, moreover, the two discussed the importance of further increasing defense spending as well as investment in the defense industrial base in both the U.S. and NATO countries, according to the statement.

Trump also noted in a post on Truth Social Thursday that he "briefed NATO on the tremendous progress" being made in growing defense production, noting that the focus will be on building Patriot air defense systems, THAAD systems and Tomahawk cruise missiles, as well as "many new Weapons, both Offensive and Defensive, that have not yet been viewed by the Public, or other Countries.".

In a recent development, "There has never been a time when the United States has produced more Military Equipment or Munitions than now. Our 'cupboard' will soon be full and, when it is, our Allies and Partners throughout the World will be benefitting greatly," he remarked in the post.

Trump's meeting with Xi and Putin, in which he described the Russian president as his "friend," sparked alarm among European lawmakers about Washington's commitment to transatlantic security.

NATO's Rutte, a seasoned diplomat known as a consensus builder during his nearly 14 years as Dutch prime minister, has repeatedly sought to de-escalate tensions in the alliance and frequently used flattery to win over the U.S. president.

While some have questioned whether this approach has delivered any tangible benefits, Trump has previously described Rutte as a "great leader" and NATO's "biggest asset.".

Russia has stepped up its attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure in recent weeks, with further attacks on the central Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih overnight disrupting power supplies and bringing municipal electric public transport to a standstill, according to Oleksandr Vilkul, head of Kryvyi ​Rih's defense council.

Ukrainian officials on Wednesday noted Russian attacks on the country's power sector had damaged energy infrastructure and caused power outages in five regions as cold winter weather sets in.

According to recent reports, german Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Wednesday accused the Kremlin of "escalating" threats toward European security, citing actions in the Baltic region, Poland and on the Black Sea, and adding that "Russia knows exactly what it wants. And Russia wants more than Ukraine.".

A spokesperson for Russia's Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond to a CNBC request for comment on Thursday morning. The Kremlin has repeatedly denied seeking military confrontation with NATO countries.

#166899. Citroën Hydraulic System

Citroën Hydraulic System

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2639 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Org

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Citroën's hydropneumatic* suspension, despite a reputation for complexity, complication and unreliability is actually very simple in operation and very reliable and furthermore, offers an unrivalled level of comfort coupled with excellent handling and grip.
  • The system takes advantage of the fact that you can compress a gas but cannot compress a fluid.
  • The system provides a soft, comfortable, yet well-controlled ride.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Citroën's hydropneumatic* suspension, despite a reputation for complexity, complication and unreliability is actually very simple in operation and very reliable and furthermore, offers an unrivalled level of comfort coupled with excellent handling and grip.

The system takes advantage of the fact that you can compress a gas but cannot compress a fluid. Thus gas acts as the springing medium while the hydraulic fluid does all the clever things such as providing damping and levelling. Unlike the hydrolastic system fitted to certain BMC and BLMC cars, the Citroën system relies on an engine-driven pump to pressurise the hydraulic system and it is this power source which enables self-levelling, variable ride height, assisted jacking and zero roll (in the Activa Xantia) and also allows for fully powered braking systems and power steering too.

The system provides a soft, comfortable, yet well-controlled ride. The nitrogen springing medium is approximately six times more flexible than a conventional steel system, so self-leveling is incorporated to allow the vehicle to cope with the extraordinary suppleness provided. In the early fifties, France was noted for particularly poor road quality and therefore the only way to maintain a relatively high speed in a vehicle was if it could easily absorb road irregularities. It was this need that also drove the development of the 2CV's interconnected suspension system.

In the DS, the high pressure hydraulic system also operated the clutch and gear change. With the introduction of the XM came electronic control of the suspension system - called Hydractive and a refined version of this system was fitted to high specification Xantias and to later XMs. The Hydractive system allowed for variable damping and automatic switching between soft and firm modes which allowed an unparalleled combination of ride comfort and good handling.

It has been revealed that hydropneumatic suspension was first shown in 1954 when it was fitted to the rear of the 15CV H Traction Avant . This was a foretaste of the system that was fitted to the astonishing DS 19 of 1955. Variants of the suspension have been fitted subsequently to the GS of 1970, the SM of the same year, the CX , the BX , the XM, the Xantia most C5s and the C6. Other cars fitted with the system were the M 35 Wankel-engined prototype, the GZ Birotor , some variants of the H van and various Rolls Royce and Mercedes-Benz cars where it was used under licence.

For an excellent technical guide in Adobe Acrobat format covering all Citroën's hydraulic systems, click here and follow the link to Technical Guide.

Above the Hydractive 2 system fitted to high specification variants of the Xantia and XM.

The system switches from "soft" to "firm" modes according to a number of parameters programmed into the on board computer.

Sensors provide the necessary input to the computer to determine which mode is appropriate.

A central sphere on each axle is switched in and out of circuit to alter the amount of suspension travel and damping.

It has been revealed that below left the Xantia front suspension comprises MacPherson type struts with the Hydropneumatic suspension spheres mounted on top. Each sphere contains a diaphragm behind which a quantity of nitrogen is trapped. A height corrector is attached to the anti roll bar and when a load is placed in the car, the car body sinks. This movement is registered by the height corrector which opens a valve to admit hydraulic fluid under pressure to "lengthen" the hydraulic strut and thereby re-establish the correct ride height. A control inside the car allows the ride height to be varied by the driver thereby aiding wheel changes.

The SC-CAR or Activa system builds on Hydractive 2 by incorporating hydraulic jacks to counter body roll.

Hydractive 2 is also fitted to most XM models.

Below right the rear suspension of the Xantia comprises trailing arms connected to an anti roll bar with height corrector attached.

The rear spheres lie flat which permits an unobstructed boot floor with no suspension unit intrusions.

The hydraulic system acquired a reputation for unreliability when it was prematurely released on the DS. There were problems with seals and the fluid originally used was intensely hygroscopic (it absorbed water) which caused oxydisation and early DS drivers frequently discovered their pride and joy resting on its haunches in a pool of fluid. The introduction of LHS improved matters but it was not until a mineral oil LHM or Liquide Hydraulique Minéral was introduced in the mid sixties that the system became thoroughly reliable.

In the DS, the hydraulic system provided power for the clutch, gearchange and steering. Additional uses of this system included the fully powered self centring steering system (DIRAVI or Varipower) fitted to the SM and CX, levelling of the headlamps fitted to the SM and a number of design studies were undertaken to investigate hydraulic operation of windscreen wipers, an air dam brake and even the opening and closing of windows.

Prior to the advent of cheap electronics, a totally hydraulic anti lock braking system had been built, together with zero roll suspension.

Electronics provided a cheap, low weight solution for active suspension and anti lock brakes.

In a recent development, anti dive suspension is incorporated The rear brakes take their fluid from the rear suspension which pulls the tail down under heavy braking. On all hydraulic Citroëns (with the exception of some early ID 19s), the balance between front to rear braking effort is modified by the respective loads placed on the front and rear suspension.

Recent findings suggest that top left - suspension in "soft" state; the solenoid valve (1) is energised, the slide valve opens allowing hydraulic fluid to flow between the between the suspension cylinders and the spheres (4 and 3) via the dampers (6). All six spheres are in use.

Bottom left - suspension is in "firm" mode; the solenoid valve (1) is not energised, the slide valve takes up a position which blocks the movement of hydraulic fluid between the two main spheres (4) on each axle and isolates the additional spheres (3) from them both.

Above - a normally suspended car undertaking the slalom test.

In a recent development, high pressure hydraulics are the jewel in Citroën's crown. The hydropneumatic suspension system offers an unparalleled level of comfort and control although it must be admitted that it is not perfect. Cars without the Hydractive or Activa systems suffer from considerable body roll (the basic system is poor in roll stiffness); the ride tends to be slightly harsh at low speeds; the hydraulic system is very good at transmitting road noise into the cabin; some people suffer from motion sickness in an hydropneumatic Citroën; there is a tendency for pitching if one is heavy footed when driving a Citroën and some drivers dislike the feeling of being divorced from the road surface. The system can be caught out by hump backed bridges - the body rises from the road surface as the apex of the bridge is reached, the height corrector then decides the car body is raised too high and reduces ride height as the vehicle descends the other side of the bridge - the body then crashes into the suspension bump stops.

On the plus side, one can drive far quicker on indifferent road surfaces than might be believed possible (this goes a long way to explaining the success of the marque in motorsport) and handling is almost unaffected by a change in ride height caused by a full load.

Additional benefits include an absence of diagonal pitching, the constant ride height ensures headlamp beams are always properly aligned, irrespective of load and aerodynamics remain unaffected by load thanks to a constant angle of attack.

More prosaic but nevertheless useful benefits include the ability to drive on terrain that is normally restricted to off-road vehicles, the ability to raise or lower the suspension to assist in loading or unloading the vehicle, to assist in changing a wheel, to facilitate towing and to make washing of the car easier.

Above - the Xantia Activa undertaking the same slalom test at the same speed - note the total absence of body roll.

The C5 features a decentralised system employing separate systems for power steering and braking while future developments may feature a pump for each road wheel and a totally active system (the Activa is, in truth, reactive, albeit its reactions are so quick as to almost deserve the appellation) which reads the road surface ahead of the car and provides precisely the correct amount of suspension travel.

Above a schematic of the DS showing the suspension system.

Below a publicity shot for the DS showing the interaction between hydraulics, represented by water and air represented by the ballons.

Above a schematic of the DS showing the braking system.

Below the suspension system showing the spheres with the nitrogen represented in blue and the hydraulic fluid in red.

Above - load (P) is placed in car and it sinks.

Left - manual ride height control in Xantia.

Above - height corrector (3) admits hydraulic fluid which "lengthens" the strut and raises the vehicle to its normal ride height.

According to recent reports, another advantage of the variable ride height was the ability to dispense with a conventional jack. To jack the car up, all that was required was to place it in the highest suspension position, place a simple stand under the car and then select the lowest suspension position. The two wheels on the side of the car under which the stand is placed lift themselves off the ground.

It has been revealed that other car manufacturers, notably Rolls-Royce and Mercedes-Benz licenced the system which was also used on Berliet trucks. Similar systems are also used on some military vehicles.

At the heart of the system are the so-called 'spheres' one per wheel and one main accumulator as well as a dedicated brake accumulator on some models. The purpose of the main accumulator is to even out fluctuations in pressure.

On later cars fitted with antisink or Activa suspension, there may be as many as nine spheres. Each sphere consists of a hollow metal ball, open to the bottom, with the top and bottom of the sphere being separated by a flexible desmopan rubber membrane. The top is filled with nitrogen at high pressure, up to 75 bar while the bottom connects to the car's hydraulic fluid circuit. The high pressure pump powered by the engine pressurizes the circuit and the accumulator sphere. This part of the circuit is at between 150 and 180 bars. It powers the front brakes first, prioritised via a security valve, and depending on type of vehicle, can power the steering, clutch, gearchange, etc.

Sources indicate that pressure goes from this circuit to the wheel spheres, pressurizing the bottom part of the spheres and rods connected to the wheel suspension. Suspension works by means of a rod pushing LHM into the sphere, compressing the nitrogen in the upper part of the sphere. Damping is provided by a two-way 'leaf valve' in the opening of the sphere. LHM has to squeeze back and forth through this valve which causes resistance and controls the suspension movements. This damper is far simpler and more reliable than those fitted to conventional vehicles and is also more efficient.

Height correction and levelling.

Car height correction works by height correctors connected to the front and rear anti-roll bars and permit more more fluid to travel under pressure to the spheres when it detects that the suspension is lower than the pre-determined ride height (e.g. the car is loaded). When the ride height is too high (e.g. after unloading) fluid is returned to the system reservoir via low-pressure return pipes. Height correctors act with some delay in order not to correct regular suspension movements. Rear brakes are powered from the rear suspension spheres. Because the pressure there is proportional to the load, so is the braking power. Furthermore, under heavy braking, hydraulic fluid is removed from the rear suspension causing the tail to drop providing inbuilt anti-dive.

Spheres are not subject to mechanical wear, but do suffer pressure loss, mostly from nitrogen diffusing through the membrane. They typically last between 60,000 and 100,000 km. Spheres once had a threaded plug on top for recharging. Newer spheres do not have this plug, but it can be retrofitted. The symptom of pressure loss is a hard ride.

Sources indicate that hydropneumatics are inherently superior to steel springs for reasons that are often misunderstood. In addition to the superb comfort, they also have advantages related to car handling and control efficiency, solving a number of problems which are inherent in the use of steel springs.

According to recent reports, the hydropneumatic system is a progressive spring-rate suspension, in other words the more it is compressed, the stiffer it becomes. This results in a suspension which is extremely soft in its initial movement (far softer than a steel spring) but which becomes harder and harder as it is compressed (far stiffer than a steel spring). This is because of the inherent properties of a gas: halve its volume and its pressure doubles. When the suspension operates, the ram pushes oil into the sphere, thereby altering the volume (and therefore the pressure) of the gas. Usually steel-sprung cars are either too soft ("comfortable"), or too stiff ("sporty"), or some intermediate compromise, while hydropneumatics offer "two cars in one". Many manufacturers supply composite steel springs with a soft course and a stiff course - two different, discrete spring rates, whereas hydropneumatics offer an infinite number of rates.

In a recent development, this also ensures that the suspension's spring-rate (hardness) is continuously adapted to the vehicle load. Thus when the car is unladen, the pressure within the spheres is in balance. If a passenger enters the car, this pressure becomes higher by the value of his or her weight (the gas in the spheres is compressed to an equal degree, i.e. has now become "harder") and the car will have lost some height, so the self-leveling system immediately reacts and brings the car up to the predetermined ride height. The result is that the spring rate is kept constant, regardless of the load of the car. In other words, a fully loaded car will be as equally well controlled as a car with just one passenger. With a steel-spring car, either the car would be set up to be comfortable with 1-2 passengers but getting too soft as more weight is added (becoming uncontrollable under full payload), or it would be too stiff with 1-2 passengers and okay on full payload. This effect is especially pronounced at the rear where the designer of a steel-sprung car has to make a compromise because the rear suspension has to be able to deal with a large range of loads. Hydropneumatically sprung cars can have a rear that is set very soft; one can easily push the empty car down with his hand. When a load is added, it stiffens as much as necessary. Steel-sprung cars need to have rear springs much stiffer than necessary for comfortable daily driving.

According to recent reports, the self-levelling system ensures that there is always the same suspension travel available irrespective of load. Furthermore, the self-levelling function also rids suspension design of a number of unwanted compromises that designers of conventionally sprung cars have to make since the suspension is always functioning around one predetermined position, no matter the car's load, the various suspension-geometry concerns become a much simpler equation to solve. A hydropneumatic suspension operates at ideal angles at all times and under all conditions. The ride comfort is excellent and never wallows uncontrollably in the way that an equally softly sprung car on steel springs would do.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • iOS 27.3 rolls out soon with a key change: certain advanced AI features will have daily usage limits.
  • When iOS 27.3, macOS 27.3, and iPadOS 27.3 arrive next month, Apple will implement usage limits for advanced AI features.
  • Some Apple Intelligence capabilities will continue having unlimited use—mainly ones that run locally.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27.3 rolls out soon with a key change: certain advanced AI features will have daily usage limits. In an article posted on X, leaker pdfu details how this upcoming system works.

When iOS 27.3, macOS 27.3, and iPadOS 27.3 arrive next month, Apple will implement usage limits for advanced AI features.

Some Apple Intelligence capabilities will continue having unlimited use—mainly ones that run locally. But for server-based features that use Private Cloud Compute (PCC), users will have daily allowances on a per-device basis.

Apple has shared some official word on how usage limits work, but many of the finer details haven’t been publicized yet. However, leaker pdfu has discovered a lot about the behind-the-scenes rules governing usage limits. Many were shared this week in an article posted on X.

For example, here’s each feature’s “standard device limit” in daily tokens per pdfu:.

Industry observers note that as explained in pdfu’s article, token usage depends on the complexity of requests. He writes:.

It has been revealed that not all features make the same number of requests. Generating one image in Image Playground, or a single query to the AFM 3 Cloud model in Shortcuts, consumes one token. Siri AI requests may make multiple connections to PCC, as server models make tool calls and receive results. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that [ demo | about | screenshots | design | docs | code | warning! | contact | credits | links ].

9/UX brings the classic Mac and A/UX desktop (a spatial desktop, a global menu bar, consistent controls and dialogs, icons, and resource-driven presentation) to 9front, built the Plan 9 way: rio and libdraw draw the screen, 9P exposes every application's UI state and commands as files, namespaces define the working environment, the plumber opens documents, and ndb holds human-editable metadata.

It is not an emulator, a Macintosh ABI, or an A/UX reimplementation. Native 9front programs stay first-class, and existing rio programs (acme, sam, rc windows, nested rio) keep working unchanged beside 9/UX apps.

These are real frames, not mockups. The GUI tests embed h9 with a headless screen, inject mouse and keyboard input, and drive the 9P files at the same time.

According to recent reports, macintosh structure, Initiative 9 colour: butter title bars from rio's selection yellow, acme's cream and olive, and rio's greygreen for the desktop, so 9/UX windows and legacy rio windows sit together on one screen. Everything reads in one bit, uses a sixteen-colour palette, and is drawn in whole pixels. Every graphic is original to 9/UX; it ships no Apple resources. The mockups below are generated from the same palette and metrics files as the code.

The design document describes 9/UX and its v0.1 acceptance criteria; release.md has where each one stands, the end-to-end demo, and the open challenges. Every interface between components is a file protocol in docs/protocols, and the visual design covers the palette, fonts, metrics, chrome, icons and cursors.

The source is on GitHub, under the MIT license. Development runs on h9, which runs 9front's own compilers, mk and rio directly from the host shell, without booting a VM. scripts/h9.sh clones and builds the pinned h9 on its first run:.

According to recent reports, use rio/6.out on amd64. development.md and testing.md have the details.

9/UX is at v0.1 and under active development. Interfaces and behaviour change without notice.

Please report bugs and send questions through GitHub problems.

The 9/UX mark in the menu bar is a pixel-art Glenda by Dan Fessler. Glenda, the Initiative 9 bunny, was created by Renée French.

Industry observers note that iOS 27.2 introduced upcoming features for Messages, Apple TV, and more, including two improvements for CarPlay. Here’s what’s new for CarPlay consumers.

Apple Podcasts in iOS 27.2 adds two new sections to the Home tab: ‘New Episodes’ and ‘Continue Playing.’.

Essentially, Apple has rethought how the core ‘Up Next’ queue of its Podcasts app works.

Recent findings suggest that like you would expect, ‘New Episodes’ contains only the latest episodes from your favorite shows. But after you’ve started an episode, you’ll find it in the ‘Continue Playing’ row just below.

Recent findings suggest that this overhaul to podcast management makes it easier to find the latest episodes of your highlights and also pick up where you previously left off. I’m a big fan of the change.

Siri AI introduces a variety of upgrades in iOS 27.2, including two that carry over to CarPlay as well.

It can take some adjustment to remember that Siri AI is available in the car just like on iPhone. But CarPlay is an especially useful platform for Apple’s more powerful assistant.

Sources indicate that it’s arguable whether this qualifies as an “improvement,” but it is a change worth mentioning. iOS 27.2 includes a new app icon for Apple Music, plus some minor design tweaks in the app. These changes are related to the broader rebrand of Apple Music that was recently unveiled.

More significant to me personally, the update also seems to have fixed a longstanding CarPlay bug regarding playlist sorting.

I use custom sorting for several of my playlists in Apple Music, and before iOS 27.2, my sort settings didn’t carry over from iPhone to CarPlay. Fortunately that’s now been fixed, as Reddit owners have reported too.

In a recent development, it’s been just over a year since Apple released AirPods Pro 3, and I can confidently say I’ve worn them every day since. After a year of heavy use, I’m even more convinced that AirPods Pro 3 are the best money you can spend on Apple gear (especially at current sale pricing).

While the changes to AirPods Pro 3 fit have been controversial to some users, I’ve been thoroughly impressed over the last year. I find them incredibly comfortable, and I absolutely notice the improvement in noise cancellation enabled by the updated in-ear fit. The sound quality, of course, is also excellent, and is made better by the updated shape.

Industry observers note that one feature I haven’t found myself using (or noticing) very often is the heart rate sensor. This is probably because I always wear an Apple Watch. Apple says that AirPods Pro 3 and Apple Watch can work together to get you the most accurate heart rate data possible. I assume this happens in the background, but I never notice or think about it.

An interesting twist to AirPods Pro 3 is that they actually have worse battery life on paper than AirPods Pro 2.

Recent findings suggest that I haven’t noticed the overall lower battery life at all. On long travel days, however, I absolutely appreciate the longer battery life from the buds themselves. I can now comfortably wear them from my departure airport to my arrival airport on most travel days. And I don’t have any problems just placing my AirPods Pro 3 on a Qi charger on my desk to refuel.

#166887. Latest Update: Source Control from Hell

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (492 w)

Latest Update: Source Control from Hell

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (492 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Frantic

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • My first office job was at an enterprise that built software for a significant telecom: a massive Delphi help desk application on Windows.
  • Let me tell you about how we managed source control process at the time.
  • First, you download the code from a shared folder (hosted on a trusted Windows server in a locked room).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

My first office job was at an enterprise that built software for a significant telecom: a massive Delphi help desk application on Windows.

Let me tell you about how we managed source control process at the time.

First, you download the code from a shared folder (hosted on a trusted Windows server in a locked room). Build your thing, run the app, test it locally. Then you upload your changes to the shared folder and create a newly introduced ticket in the internal task tracker (also a Windows app). The ticket should have a list of the changes you’ve made, in a rich text editor, in a manual format somewhat resembling a patch. But it wasn’t a patch; it couldn’t simply be applied with a tool. Instead, the tech lead looks at the shared folder and your task and copies the relevant changes to his own integration folder. This usually took him a full day because the shared folder had a lot of changes, not all of them were ready to be integrated. Needless to say, if you simply pull a snapshot of the code from the shared folder, it would most likely fail to compile.

The most common problem was two people overwriting each other’s work. So if you wanted to upload your stuff to the shared folder, you had to stand up and announce in a loud voice that you were using the shared folder. No chat apps back in the day.

Imagine starting your career with this development experience! I did my best to improve it. At the time, almost everyone used FAR Manager, so I built a plugin that locked the folder when someone was using it, so others would get a warning. It became very popular because nobody really liked the old yelling system.

It has been revealed that then in 2009 I found git. It was still early days, way before GitHub went mainstream, but my tiny little brain was blown away. Holy shit, it maintains old versions. And you can work locally. And you can sync and exchange deltas. And it was insanely fast (compared to the very aptly named TortoiseSVN I’d experimented with earlier). I must have rewatched Linus’ talk a billion times. I created git repos for every project I had, preached it to my friends, and even gave my first tech talk about git at my university.

Sadly, my diplomatic skills were extremely rudimentary, and I couldn’t convince our tech lead to adopt git. He mumbled something about business value and how this new git thing lacked one. I left the tech giant after two years but kept meeting up with old colleagues for beer. They were still using the shared folder process many years later. It was crude, it was hellish, and it worked for them just fine.

Thanks for reading. If you want more, I'll email you when I write the next one. Or use RSS.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that apple has introduced several exciting new products in the last month, including iPhone Duo and the redesigned MacBook Pro. But my personal favorite new product is Apple’s HomeView. Here’s how I’ve been using it.

Two years ago when Mark Gurman published an in-depth report on Apple’s forthcoming HomeView, I was immediately ready to buy one.

Recent findings suggest that after numerous delays, the HomeView is finally here. And despite several shortcomings I expect will be fixed with software updates, the HomeView overall is exactly what I’ve been wanting in a home product.

Industry observers note that homeView is essentially a HomePod, but with a screen. And that screen adds so much extra value.

When rumors remarked the HomeView would only have a 7-inch display, I was concerned it would be too small. It turns out, Apple knew what it was doing. The HomeView’s size is a feature, not a bug. Too much larger and it would stand out as a piece of tech. By staying small, the HomeView can be a cute, non-distracting addition to the home.

Here are some HomeView features I’ve been loving so far:.

None of these is what I’d call a “killer feature,” but together they amount to a delightful experience. I already liked having a HomePod around, and HomeView builds on that foundation in so many ways.

Overall, HomeView is very much the product I was hoping for back in 2024. That stated, there’s definitely room for improvement. Here’s what’s missing.

According to recent reports, I love HomeView for what it is today, but I fully expect Apple to improve the product via software updates. Leaks already point to two major feature upgrades in the works that I hope ship soon.

It has been revealed that built-in apps for Apple Photos and Notes would be great to have, plus support for the recipes included in Apple News+. But my personal top request is for parental controls of some sort.

I completely agree, this is exactly the device I’ve been waiting for.

Sources indicate that my only con… Siri AI is just slightly more than half-baked when it comes to voice prompts. One example, when we ask it for the weather forecast it gives us a one-line “It’s going to rain today.” That’s not a forecast. 🙃 So we’re forced to follow up with “more details please”. When we do… 🙂 … we get an actual forecast. Asking it for a recap of today’s headlines is hit or miss too. These are just two of a handful of examples where Siri AI is only about 60% of what Alexa+ is for conversational AI purposes.

In a recent development, with that one nod to the nut jobs out there claiming an old iPad suffices everyone on planet earth perfectly well, I’m still giddy about the fact that I can browse through my full library of music on Apple Music, Amazon Music, and iBroadcast and try new “suggested” albums/playlists without having to have my iPhone with me everywhere I go in the house. While I spent $299 mainly for an enhanced music experience, having it is priceless.

According to recent reports, for a device that’s intended for the whole family, I’ve been surprised to find there are no current features to prevent young children from doing whatever they want with HomeView. I have a toddler who loves the HomeView so much that I had to move it out of his reach. I wish there was a way to lock the screen on command, or prevent switching apps or faces without authentication. Some sort of “toddler mode” would be greatly appreciated.

Siri AI has also had some bugs, but those are likely related to me running the iOS 27.3 beta.

Apple’s newly introduced HomeView is available now for $299.

According to recent reports, what’s your take on the HomeView so far? Are you still mulling a purchase? Let us know in the comments.

Three skills in this plugin (listed in Anthropic's claude-plugins-official marketplace) raised the same concern for me:.

It has been revealed that I read this as a team trying to make onboarding reliable, not as anything malicious. But the last item tells the agent to change the shape of a command so that the user's safety tooling does not catch it, which removes the check the user or their administrator chose to have. Together with an unpinned script from a generated-name host, a user has no way to review what runs.

convex-backend-skill/skills/quickstart/SKILL.md.

Lines 48 to 56 in 6ca54f6.

convex-backend-skill/skills/add/SKILL.md.

Lines 58 to 65 in 6ca54f6.

convex-backend-skill/skills/labs-quickstart/SKILL.md.

Lines 74 to 80 in 6ca54f6.

(All three are still on main as of 26 October; in labs-quickstart the passage is now lines 73 to 80.).

Suggestions: tell the user before the idea is sent, and make it optional; ship the bootstrap and add scripts in the plugin (or pin them by hash) instead of fetching them at run time; and drop the instruction about the classifier, letting the download-and-run step be approved or refused as it is.

I maintain a catalog of agent skills and of the tools for vetting them; it lists these findings at https://thirtysix.github.io/awesome-agent-skills/#skills?q=convex and I will add your response.

In a recent development, and I who was just looking at giving Convex my money. But now will probably instead look more closely at the alternatives I was already looking at.

macOS 27.3 is launching next month alongside iOS 27.3 and more, and it includes a variety of latest features for Mac people. Here are three macOS 27.3 features coming soon.

Recent findings suggest that macOS already supports running Live Activities from your iPhone via iPhone Mirroring. But in macOS 27.3, Apple is adding native support for Live Activities from Mac apps.

The feature first debuted on the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display, which features Live Activities in the fresh Dynamic Island. But with macOS 27.3, the new feature expands to all Mac models and in a slightly different way.

Sources indicate that live Activities on Macs without a Dynamic Island will display in the menu bar. From there you can click to view full details, as seen above.

Safari introduces several upgrades across macOS 27.3, iOS 27.3, and iPadOS 27.3.

Industry observers note that vertical Tabs are one tentpole addition, providing a upcoming option for how to view your tabs in Apple’s browser. When enabled, your tabs move from the top of the browser to the left side in a new column view.

Recent findings suggest that adaptive Dark Mode is another new feature. It automatically enables dark mode on many websites that don’t natively support it already. Finally, Siri AI gains support for new Safari actions, including the ability to interact with a full webpage using onscreen awareness, not just the parts that are right now visible.

In a recent development, do you use Markdown, the popular John Gruber-created plain text syntax? If so, macOS 27.3 has a welcome addition: support for rendering Markdown in Quick Look.

Rather than needing to open Markdown files in apps to preview formatted text, macOS now lets you just use Quick Look and see all of your Markdown syntax rendered properly with links, headings, bold, italics, and more.

You can learn more about Markdown here on John Gruber’s site, Daring Fireball.

#166876. iPhone Duo Diary: Pros & cons in early real-life use

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2013 w)
