According to recent reports, developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it. A new feature from Anthropic is banking on more adventurous, agent-first coders being comfortable with handing even that last step off to AI.

With Claude Ship, revealed in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic said. The feature is geared toward individual developers or companies who want to move faster or already delegate a significant amount of coding tasks to agents.

Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.

Industry observers note that “Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person,” Anthropic said. “The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”.

The new feature uses two new agents alongside Code Review, which Anthropic released in March for Teams and Enterprise plans. Code Review first collects, organizes, and posts findings to a PR. Then, Anthropic mentioned, the agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, guide a PR “through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually.”.

According to recent reports, PR Steward can’t approve or merge pull requests, designed instead to participate “on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members.” It also documents what it changed in each push through comments and provides instructions for how to undo it, should developers want to. Throughout the process, developers can give Claude instructions or tell it to stop by commenting @claude.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free – how it went.

Industry observers note that as a final step, Claude Approvals references whatever policy the user or team abides by (which developers provide as a repo file), and additional signals developers set, like Code Review findings, before approving changes autonomously if allowed. If not, it will seek out “deeper human sign-off,” Anthropic mentioned.

“It works like a smarter CODEOWNERS file,” the release added. Anthropic mentioned it recommends that most customers enable those additional checks “first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals’ green light.”.

Admins can select which repos the feature runs in and adjust settings as needed.

But Claude Ship isn’t meant for everyone.

“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” Anthropic stated in the release, noting that its own Claude Code team uses Claude to write a majority of the code it needs.

ZDNET senior contributing editor David Gewirtz said the idea of shipping code at the speed of writing it “raises the hair on the back of my neck.” But he added that, given how impressive Claude Code has been thus far, he wouldn’t be surprised if Anthropic’s deployment tools were equally effective.

Sources indicate that also: Claude Code vs. Codex: Why I use both and how to choose one (if you must).

“But, it does depend on the team’s workflow and the kind of development they’re doing,” he remarked. “It’s not something for every team and certainly not for every indy developer, but for certain deployment processes, it could shave a ton of time off turnaround, saving money and potentially sending fixes to customers much faster. ‘Tis cool.”.

Ultimately, Gewirtz noted he has reasons to both trust the tool and be concerned about what it means for younger developers in the workplace.

“Since that workflow is often assigned to less experienced members of the team, it’s likely that Claude would be as accurate, although it’s one more way to shut the junior members out of where they add value to the organization and grow their skills to become senior decision makers,” he noted.

According to recent reports, developer platforms overall are adapting to the new state of the industry. Entire, a GitHub competitor started by the Microsoft-owned platform’s former CEO, is built around the expectation that developers are working side-by-side with agents.

According to recent reports, individuals with a Pro, Max, or Ultra subscription can use the /ship command now available in Claude Code, meaning “owners won’t notice any significant increase in token usage,” an Anthropic representative explained. Team and Enterprise users can use Claude Ship for Github repos, and it is billed on tokens, so your overall bill may change.

In a recent development, still, that depends on the number of PRs people are putting through Claude Ship — to avoid any surprises, admins can set spending limits for both Code Review and the upcoming PR Steward agent. They can also turn Claude Ship on for an entire repo, meaning developers won’t need the /ship command.

It has been revealed that anthropic added that certain Enterprise organizations “can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits to use within 30 days of claiming” by Jan. 15, 2027.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac – with Claude Code standing guard.

As with other Claude features, like the still-to-come Meetings, customers with a zero-data-retention policy and other privacy configurations don’t have access to Claude Ship.

  • Sources indicate that thanksgiving is almost here, as is Cyber Monday, but soon it’ll be officially winter.
  • Sources indicate that the winter solstice has a few different meanings, so here are all of them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that this was taken with the main camera as a ProRaw photo. Notice the lights on the tree, compared to the green hue of the street lighting and blue and pink tones in the sky.

Sources indicate that thanksgiving is almost here, as is Cyber Monday, but soon it’ll be officially winter. The winter solstice is on Dec. 21, when we’ll experience Earth’s shortest, darkest day.

Sources indicate that the winter solstice has a few different meanings, so here are all of them. The most common definition, and the one you’re most likely familiar with, is that it denotes the shortest day and longest night of the year on Earth. These times vary depending on your location on the globe, but the further north you live, the less sunlight you’ll get. In the tropics, they’ll get about 12 hours of sunlight. In Sweden, it’ll be closer to 6 hours. In Svalbard, there isn’t any.

Sources indicate that the reason this occurs is due to the second definition of the winter solstice: During this time, the North Pole is tilted as far away from the sun as it can get. According to The Farmer’s Almanac, the moment at which the Earth’s axis is physically tilted as much as it can be is at 3:50 p.m. ET on Monday, Dec. 21. After that moment, the process will begin to reverse until the South Pole takes its turn during the summer solstice. At that point, the North Pole will be at its closest tilt to the sun, giving us the longest day and shortest night of the year for the Northern Hemisphere.

It has been revealed that sunset will occur at its earliest time on Dec. 21.

It’ll vary by location. The southern US will have the most sunlight, with Florida getting a little over 10 hours during the winter solstice. The Midwest and Great Lakes portion of the country will get roughly nine hours. The Pacific Northwest can expect a little less than nine hours. Southern Alaska will get about six hours, and the northern areas of Alaska will see around three hours.

Industry observers note that if you want to see how your area will fare, Time and Date has a sunrise and sunset tool you can use. Input your zip code into the search bar, and you’ll be able to see your sunrise and sunset times.

It has been revealed that the city of Utqiaġvik, Alaska, will have it worse than most in the US: It won’t get any sun at all. The sun won’t rise there again until late January. We hope the people living there packed their vitamin D supplements.

The autumn equinox was just a couple of months ago, so you may be curious about the differences. A solstice occurs when the Earth’s poles are tilted as far away from the sun as they’ll be over the course of one year, which is also one orbit around the sun. The equinoxes take place at the halfway points between each solstice. The autumn equinox takes place in September between the summer and winter solstices, while the spring equinox takes place in March between the winter and summer.

During an equinox, the poles are minimally tilted, and the days are as even as they can be. This also has a couple of other interesting side effects: The sun is pointed directly at the equator during an equinox, and the sun will rise and set directly east and west, respectively.

Sources indicate that humans use the solstices and equinoxes to mark the change of the seasons. There are two equinoxes and two solstices, which mark the start and end dates for Earth’s four seasons.

Decorating with evergreen trees, like with a wreath, is what they used to do to celebrate the winter solstice.

Recent findings suggest that while the solstice is close to the holidays, celebrations for the winter solstice have been around for significantly longer, and some winter solstice traditions have become Christmas traditions as well. One of the most historically famous winter solstice celebrations is Yule, a winter festival originating thousands of years ago among the ancient Norse. It became commonly celebrated in Europe and involved bonfires and massive feasts. Yule celebrations also included decorating with evergreen tree decorations, like holly and ivy.

In a recent development, if these sound familiar, it’s because Christmas co-opted many of those traditions centuries ago, and the two traditions have kind of merged into a single seasonal holiday. The terms Yule and Christmas are often used interchangeably these days in many cultures.

So if you want to celebrate the winter solstice, just do all of the stuff you would normally do for the holidays. Burn a Yule log, decorate a tree, eat a big feast with your family and hang up mistletoe and wreaths — those are all hat tips to traditional winter solstice celebrations.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another.
  • Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.
  • According to recent reports, because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another. For example, many ships sail in the Mediterranean Sea during the summer and move to the Caribbean Sea for the winter, and that trip between the two is a repositioning cruise.

Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.

According to recent reports, because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea. For some travelers, that’s a chance to relax and enjoy the ship’s onboard amenities. Sometimes, these sailings can also be cheaper than traditional cruises.

Sources indicate that one key consideration for a repositioning cruise is that the embarkation and disembarkation ports will be different. This means you generally can’t buy a standard round-trip flight to and from the same city. Instead, you’ll need transportation to where the cruise starts and another way home from where it ends, which usually means two one-way flights (or one open-jaw ticket) unless you live near one of the ports. While these one-way sailings may be more affordable than traditional cruises, airfare costs may be higher.

This could be a great opportunity to redeem miles for your flight.

Another feature that sets these cruises apart is that stops along the way tend to include ports that aren’t traditionally part of regular itineraries. These might include islands like Bermuda, the Azores or the Canary Islands, and on some northern routes, Greenland.

It has been revealed that just keep in mind that the main purpose of these sailings is to get to a new region for the next season’s itineraries rather than make daily port stops. So if you’re someone who wants to visit as many places as possible on a cruise, a repositioning sailing may not be the ideal choice.

Repositioning cruises are often longer than standard cruises, commonly running two to three weeks compared with about a week for a typical sailing, which may appeal to travelers looking for an extended vacation. The experience is often more relaxed, with many days at sea and less of a rush to book shore excursions or visit important sites when off the ship.

If there are particular ships with certain amenities — like tattoo parlors or massive waterparks — that you really want to experience, keep in mind that not all ships reposition between regions. Some stay in certain regions year-round.

For ships that do change locations for the season, there are plenty of onboard activities to fill the time. You can enjoy shows, food and wine tastings, organized activities and time at the spa, pool or casino.

Industry observers note that many repositioning crossings are relatively smooth, and modern ships use stabilizers to reduce movement. But since these itineraries cross open ocean rather than staying closer to land, there can be more motion, especially on North Atlantic crossings in fall and winter.

Industry observers note that if you tend to get seasick, this could be a dealbreaker. Even if a repositioning sailing is smooth, temperatures can be chilly on the open ocean, especially on northerly or spring and fall transatlantic routes, with strong winds that may make suntanning by the pool less appealing.

In a recent development, you can book one of these sailings in the same way you would book a traditional cruise. But if you’re searching for dates and itineraries on a cruise line’s website, they may be listed as transatlantic, transpacific or Panama Canal sailings rather than repositioning cruises, though some lines do use the term "repositioning." There’s even a website that specializes in rounding up these cruises: RepoCruises.com.

Recent findings suggest that keep an eye out for themed sailings that focus on topics like wine, theater or music, where fellow guests on the ship may share similar interests. Cruise lines often schedule them on repositioning cruises to spur demand.

According to recent reports, here are some repositioning cruises for 2027. They often take place during shoulder seasons, between the most popular cruising times in places like the Mediterranean or Caribbean.

  • The FTC complaint alleges that Shein failed to follow through on its swift shipping policies, made it difficult for customers to resolve purchase problems and stifled negative customer reviews from seeing the light of day.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shein, one of the biggest fast-fashion brands in the world, has been ordered to pay $100 million by the Federal Trade Commission, which alleges that the Singapore-based online retail giant engaged in deceptive practices that left millions of US customers dissatisfied with its products and policies.

The FTC complaint alleges that Shein failed to follow through on its swift shipping policies, made it difficult for customers to resolve purchase problems and stifled negative customer reviews from seeing the light of day.

The complaint also alleges problems with the organization’s supply chain, false information about the origin of the cotton used in its clothes, a failure to communicate shipping updates to customers and a lack of support for those whose packages were late or went missing altogether.

“The company misled millions of consumers about its products, its suppliers and the authenticity of its customer reviews,” Christopher Mufarrige, director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection, said in a statement on Tuesday.

Shein has ballooned over the past decade into the ultra-fast-fashion brand we know today, thanks in large part to the impact influencers have had on social media, posting videos trying on clothing supplied by the company.

It has been revealed that in 2026, the company is estimated to ship roughly 1 million packages to US customers daily, according to the FTC. That number becomes even more astounding when you consider that Shein, the FTC alleges, employed just five customer service agents to answer calls from American customers.

This isn’t the first time Shein has faced negative scrutiny. Over the years, the organization has faced allegations of numerous workers’ rights violations and is the largest polluter in the fast-fashion industry.

According to Yale Climate Connections, the manufacturer emitted 16.7 million total metric tons of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere in 2023. Comparatively speaking, that’s more than the pollution output of four coal power plants. Shein has since pledged to improve its treatment of workers and reduce carbon emissions, but scrutiny persists.

Recent findings suggest that the $100 million will be used to compensate customers. And according to the FTC’s proposed order, the firm, which earned roughly $50 billion in revenue in 2025, will not be able to continue advertising inaccurate shipping and delivery times; negative reviews will no longer be hidden; and its customer service offering will be bolstered.

“The agreement does not constitute an admission of liability, and we continue to disagree with aspects of the FTC’s characterization of our business and compliance practices,” a Shein spokesperson told CNET.

Doorbell cameras may seem like a good way to make a porch thief think twice, but the reality doesn’t quite match up. Some porch pirates don’t care about being caught on camera as long as they’re able to steal your package, and it’s unlikely that law enforcement will track down the stolen goods.

That’s the case for my fellow CNET editor, Gael Cooper, who had her Amazon delivery stolen a few weeks ago and spotted the thief on camera. It wasn’t expensive tech or a snazzy holiday gift — it was $36 worth of soda.

“When Amazon emailed me that the order was delivered and it wasn’t there, I was very confused,” Cooper said. “When I pulled up the Ring footage, I saw the delivery happen on video, but then, 10 minutes later, a man in a blue hooded coat who’s intentionally hiding his face shows up and grabs the box.”.

Recent findings suggest that package theft cases like this happen year-round, with CNET findings showing that 28% of US adults have had a package stolen, know someone who has or have stopped an attempted theft. And experts predict more stolen packages during the holidays, when thieves expect more deliveries.

It has been revealed that so, don’t give thieves a chance. Now’s the time to make a proposal to keep your Black Friday and Cyber Monday packages out of sight. But what tactics actually work if doorbell cameras don’t? Here’s what you should know about porch piracy and how to lessen your chances of package theft.

Cooper’s Amazon order was scheduled to arrive between 3 a.m. and 6 a.m. — when it’s dark, but she knew she would be home. But thieves were already out lurking during those hours. Cooper noted the thief followed the driver and stole the package. She saw the thief stealing the package on her Ring security camera system.

Greg Zakowicz, Omnisend’s e-commerce and retail advisor, mentioned Cooper’s package-theft incident is fairly typical, unfortunately — especially during the holiday season.

“Thieves know as well as shoppers that orders increase during this time, and often, the packages are more likely to contain more valuable items,” said Zakowicz. “Shoppers during this time look to take advantage of deep discounts for not only gifts but themselves, making the package a potential goldmine for thieves.”.

There are a few steps you can take to lessen the likelihood of porch piracy. Zakowicz recommends using options like in-store pickups, post office boxes, in-garage delivery or deliveries to your workplace.

That advice is especially crucial for expensive tech you strategy to have delivered to your home unless someone will be there to grab the package immediately.

“While it may be less convenient, it’s a small price to pay to not have the hassle of gifts and expensive items going missing at the busiest shopping time of the year,” noted Zackowicz.

It has been revealed that also ask your retailers not to ship the item in the manufacturer’s packaging. Some retailers, like Amazon and Target, will clearly display this before shipping because it could be an easy hint for thieves to guess what it is — especially if it’s tech. Even though this won’t stop porch pirates from being curious about what’s in the box, it may make them think about the effort and risk versus the potential reward, Zakowicz stated.

If you want another option to have packages delivered to your home, consider scheduling your deliveries for a time you know you’ll be available. For instance, you can set up an Amazon Day to have all of your Amazon packages delivered at once so you can blueprint accordingly.

CNET found that US adults have mixed feelings about how effectively security cameras deter porch pirates: 11% of US adults believe they don’t deter them, while 9% use security cameras to get proof — not prevent it.

According to recent reports, regardless of your home security measures, don’t assume you’re safe from porch pirates just because you have a doorbell camera, and don’t use it as a means of keeping an eye on your package if you’re busy or not home. Instead, when you see motion detection, that’s a sign to grab it right away.

Recent findings suggest that “The most common misunderstanding is that having security cameras will prevent thieves from stealing packages,” said Zakowicz. “Thieves are thieves because being caught is not their biggest worry. They also know porch piracy is not at the top of most officers’ day-to-day public service worries. Often, by the time the report is made, thieves are long gone.”.

It has been revealed that unfortunately, thieves may find other ways to steal packages, since their tactics are constantly changing. If that happens to you, there are a few steps you should take right away.

In a recent development, file a police report of the incident first. Be prepared to share information, including a description of the thief, and the make and model of the vehicle, with the police and your community so they can be vigilant of the thief.

Industry observers note that but don’t get your hopes up that the thief will be caught. Zakowicz stated it’s rare that porch theft cases get solved.

Industry observers note that “Police aren’t necessarily dedicating resources to solving porch pirates who stole a newly introduced stuffed animal or board game. However, it’s important for them to understand areas seeing an uptick in thefts, as they can be more alert to suspicious activity,” remarked Zakowicz. And the retailer may request it.

After filing, Zakowicz claims to report the theft to the carrier and retailer. Carriers may use the data to assess future likelihood of package theft incidents and it could help instruct delivery drivers to carefully hide packages. Retailers may also be able to assist with a replacement.

Cooper filed a police report with her local police department, which allowed her to upload the Ring video of the theft and acknowledged receipt. She’s not expecting the thief to be caught, but figures that her report could possibly help in some way.

“I live in a pretty safe neighborhood in Amazon’s own hometown, but their delivery trucks are on our street dropping off packages every day,” she remarked. “It’s got to be a banquet for hungry thieves.”.

She reached out to her neighbors to tell them about the theft, and one reported that she, too, had had a package stolen a week earlier.

It has been revealed that cooper says she did not intentionally choose the early-morning drop-off time, but it was the only time Amazon offered for her delivery. Since then, she’s seen Amazon try to offer that same time and has chosen not to order an item rather than be forced to use that dark, quiet delivery slot.

Sources indicate that immediately after the theft, Amazon was less than helpful, routing her to an AI agent who noted it understood the situation was upsetting but that it wouldn’t be able to do anything for four days. When she checked back, Amazon agreed to refund her for the item, but kept insisting on labeling the package as “missing” and asked her to report back if she “found” it.

According to recent reports, “I hope the driver doesn’t get in trouble for a supposedly ‘missing’ package,” she noted. “It unnerves me that she was being followed by a thief. Who knows how long he followed that truck and how many packages he scooped up?”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that generation Z might have the lowest morale around AI at work compared to other generations. That’s according to a survey from talent services firm Seramount, which found that Gen Z was the most AI-averse among the generations surveyed about using the technology in their jobs.

Gen Z, which includes those born between 1997 and 2012, expressed the least interest and found the least utility in AI, Seramount found. Only 18% of Gen Z reported an interest in strengthening their AI skills, compared to 36% of Millennials, 46% of Gen Xers, and 43% of Boomers. Gen Z is also using AI less than other generations, by nine percentage points.

Also: OpenAI is offering small businesses free AI support – and up to $8K/mo to experts who help them.

“Employers cannot assume their youngest employees will embrace AI on their own,” said Diana Forster, senior director of research at Seramount.

The survey polled responses from over 1,800 US white-collar workers at companies with at least 500 employees.

Recent findings suggest that around half of Gen Z report weekly AI use (not specific to work), according to a survey from Walton Family Foundation, GSV Ventures and Gallup, but the generation’s skepticism has mounted over the past few years. Even members of Gen Z who use AI daily have less positive views on the technology. In the same study, 42% of Gen Z reported feeling anxious about AI in 2026, a 1% increase from 2025. Last year, 36% of Gen Z respondents reported excitement about AI. In 2026, that percentage dropped to 22%.

Also: These companies are actually upskilling their workers for AI – here’s how they do it.

In a recent development, it’s no surprise Gen Z is skeptical about adopting a technology that could be undermining their own career development. The labor market has been particularly harsh to this group of workers, as entry-level job postings have fallen in recent years, and many fear that AI will only exacerbate unemployment. Around 8% of those ages 22 to 24 were unemployed in September, compared to 3% of workers ages 25 to 54, according to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

But with many workplaces still adopting AI, senior employees are trying to prepare Gen Z by getting them on board at work.

“We need to show young workers how AI can strengthen their work, provide clear guidelines and training, and give them opportunities to practice using it and build the skills they’ll need as leaders,” Forster remarked.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the latest and greatest home security products often start at your front door, and for good reason. That’s where burglars first try, too, and research indicates thieves can be deterred with the presence of a security cam — but security technology can do so much more.

Industry observers note that from protecting packages to managing access the smart way, here are the devices I use every day to guard my front door, and I couldn’t imagine my home without. Take a look to see what your porch could use, too, and the tech options I recommend looking at.

Industry observers note that old deadbolts do well, but any entryway can get a powerful upgrade by adding digital features via a smart lock. Smart locks allow you to control your front door lock from anywhere using your phone, as well as creating temporary passes for guests. They can support digital wallet keys for touchless unlocking, and many have keypads or fingerprint readers. Plus, you can enable settings like auto-locking, so you never have to worry about forgetting to lock the door.

Industry observers note that smart locks come in two flavors: retrofits that leave your deadbolt largely intact and only replace your indoor thumb turn, and full deadbolt replacements that give you latest locking power, inside and out. Don’t worry about installation: If you’ve never installed a deadbolt before, the process is generally easy and doesn’t take much time. I have a full guide where you can find more details.

In a recent development, say goodbye to dusty doorbells of the past. Today’s high-tech doorbells do far more than chime: Video doorbells keep an eye on your front porch, while also giving you a two-way audio intercom right on your phone to hold a conversation — or even let an LLM do the talking for you.

Video doorbells also have particularly useful object recognition features, sometimes even for free. That includes recognizing packages and alerting you whenever one shows up at your door, or when one suddenly vanishes. Video storage options can save recordings of key events, so you can check who came to the door if you need to.

Sources indicate that these advanced doorbells come in both wired and wireless versions. I’m a fan of the battery-powered, wireless models, which you can set and angle to get just the right look at your porch, doormat and other key places. Many can also work with your current door chime, although you probably don’t need it anymore with phone-based chimes.

Yale’s delivery boxes are larger, so you need room for them in the right spots.

Package theft concerns have reignited a centuries-old tradition of protecting mail. Today’s modern delivery boxes are specifically designed to allow delivery people to put packages inside, but make it difficult or impossible for thieves to take packages out, through clever lock models, auto-locking, smart controls and other various tricks.

I’ve been using a delivery box myself for a couple of years and find it very handy, as long as you have the space by your door. Some versions even come weighted or screwed down if you’re worried about a porch pirate absconding with the entire box. It’s a good idea to put notes in your deliveries to use the box, since despite signs not all delivery people will notice it’s there.

As a final plus, these boxes also keep your packages protected from the elements, which is nice when you live in an area that gets frequent winter snowstorms, as I do.

Smart bulbs are cheap, support multiple voice assistants and have lots of fun tricks.

Recent findings suggest that where front doors exist, there’s usually a light nearby, like an overhead porch light or a wall-mounted lamp, to illuminate the entryway and surrounding area. These lights can also get a major makeover if you switch to an LED smart bulb, which are available as both BR30 floodlights and standard A19 home bulbs.

It has been revealed that these lights also give you phone app controls, which is more vital than it might seem. With my apps, I can control brightness, set schedules for bulbs to turn on or off, and even adjust the color to whatever I want, say for a holiday event. All it takes is screwing in the bulb and connecting it to Wi-Fi, so you can be done in seconds.

Industry observers note that if you feel like experimenting, you can usually link smart bulbs to other devices, too. For example, you could set the light to turn on automatically when a smart lock is unlocked, or when a security system is disarmed.

Now that your front porch is up to date, take a look at the latest home AI tricks I’ve found are actually worth using and how to get them.

  • Recent findings suggest that anthropic first released artifacts in 2024.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that anthropic is making its Claude artifacts available as desktop apps, meaning you can share and more easily access your most-repeated tasks on your computer. The “install as app” feature is available in beta for all free and paid Claude prepares and works on both Mac and Windows, but not Linux.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

Recent findings suggest that anthropic first released artifacts in 2024. Since then, they’ve become a way to standardize and repeat tasks people do regularly, especially at work. Previously, artifacts ran via your Claude window or in a browser. By splicing them out as distinct desktop apps, you can now run different Claude queries while also using your artifacts locally, or use those apps without opening Claude at all.

“When an artifact is installed as a Mac or Windows app, it gets its own icon and opens in its own window instead of inside Claude. You can share it with others, and it needs your permission before it can interact with your computer,” Anthropic said.

Artifact apps can still access Claude and any connectors you’re using, and they update automatically when you edit the artifact itself in Claude. When apps request something from Claude, though, that goes toward your Claude usage limits, which are lowest for free people.

Anthropic said the app feature is meant to streamline building apps for both developer and non-developer work.

Also: Can AI plan terrorist attacks? US tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok.

The patch clarifies where AI software for work is headed. Claude is already more of an AI-powered work suite than a single helpful chatbot for many organizations. Evidently, people are using tools like artifacts frequently enough — and simultaneously with other Claude features — that they need those Claude-based tools to function like discrete bits of software on their own.

“If you rely on a tool for work, it should open like the rest of your apps and remind you when something needs your attention,” Anthropic remarked.

Claude artifact apps don’t have the same functionality as apps you could build using Claude Code, though. Even if you don’t need Claude open for these apps to work, you’ll still need to be signed in to Claude and have internet access, so they’re not an entirely portable or off-grid option.

The feature’s support page also notes that legacy artifacts, “live artifacts from Claude Cowork,” and artifacts generated from templates like Docs, Slides, and Sheets can’t be installed as desktop apps.

It has been revealed that first, make sure Claude for Mac or Windows is updated. You can try the “install as app” feature, which is in beta for all free and paid plans, via Claude’s Share menu. Select the Install as app option, which will then download the artifact you chose to your desktop. From there, set permissions as needed.

Permissions range from the default (whatever they are in a browser) to app-specific permissions like sending notifications and full computer access.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free.

Full computer access means the artifact app can “run programs and read, change, or delete your files without asking each time,” Anthropic noted, so proceed carefully. Every time you edit and patch the artifact (and thus the app), Claude will ask you to confirm permissions again, so you’ll ideally have regular checkpoints to revise access. Still, there are some guardrails in place: Anthropic only lets you give full computer access to apps you’ve made yourself. For Team and Enterprise aims, that extends to any apps made by your coworkers.

“Anthropic doesn’t review apps before you install them, so only give full access to apps you trust,” the company mentioned.

For Claude Enterprise plans, the install-as-app feature is off entirely until an admin turns it on in Organization settings.

Apple Brings Its iPhone Broadcasting to Formula 1 at the Las Vegas Grand Prix

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that when you watch a Formula 1 race on TV, the screen is packed with lap times, driver stats and real-time video from inside the cars and around the track.
  • According to recent reports, using iPhone cameras for big events is no longer a novelty.
  • Industry observers note that but compared to a ballpark, F1 ratchets up the complexity, especially in Las Vegas.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that when you watch a Formula 1 race on TV, the screen is packed with lap times, driver stats and real-time video from inside the cars and around the track. During the Las Vegas Grand Prix race, some of those views were captured with iPhone Pro phones and transmitted in real time over T-Mobile’s 5G network.

According to recent reports, using iPhone cameras for big events is no longer a novelty. Apple has been shooting its event videos and ad spots with iPhone Pro models outfitted with cinema-grade lenses, SSD storage and broadcasting gear for several years now. In May, Apple broadcast a Major League Soccer game shot with iPhones strapped to professional lenses, following it up with a Major League Baseball game in September using its own camera hardware,.

Industry observers note that but compared to a ballpark, F1 ratchets up the complexity, especially in Las Vegas. At the Las Vegas Grand Prix, the race track snakes 3.9 miles through the city’s downtown core. Its route includes the famed Strip (South Las Vegas Boulevard), where most of the big hotels are.

In a recent development, “We control everything on baseball, so we can do whatever we want there,” stated Royce Dickerson, executive producer of live sports at Apple TV. “We did 14 iPhones on top of our normal camera complement” during the baseball broadcast. He noted that 10 of those were connected via T-Mobile’s 5G wireless network.

But integrating iPhone cameras into an F1 broadcast, even for the sport’s US broadcaster, is more of a challenge. “I’ve been doing TV production for 20-plus years,” said Dickerson, “and the scale of their operation is unlike anything I’ve seen before.”.

It has been revealed that because F1 has agreements with other camera partners, Dickerson did not specify how many iPhones were set up around the track. Neither Apple nor T-Mobile explained where the iPhones were placed in order to capture the speedy F1 vehicles racing around the Vegas Strip. I suspect they were likely deployed in more conventional environments for smartphone cameras, like the team garages and roving to catch celebrities in the paddock area and in the stands, though the iPhone setups wirelessly broadcasting footage at earlier sporting events means they could be easily placed in many locations on and above the streets.

“You really have to work hard to earn the fans’ attention [and] that viewing experience,” remarked Dickerson. “How are you getting your fans closer to their favorite athlete, to their favorite driver, to their team, to the personalities that surround the sport?”.

It has been revealed that in the T-Mobile zone at the Sphere – an area sponsored by the carrier and open to T-Mobile customers – at least 10 iPhone cameras were used to cover a stage where concerts played between events. That number is based on a diagram shared during a tour of T-Mobile’s Tech Trailer, where the company’s event coordinators stay on top of things like crowd movements and line lengths.

Dean Locke, executive director of broadcast, media and race operations at Formula 1, sees the combination of multiple cameras streaming wirelessly over 5G as an essential component to the Las Vegas race.

Recent findings suggest that “If we just did cameras at a low level, the fences and track, we haven’t done a very good job,” stated Locke. “How can we open up stages, concerts and all of the activities? Each race has a real kind of personality to it. You can only [capture that personality] with huge amounts of cameras, huge amounts of technology.”.

If Apple is using iPhones to record live sports, are they recording any of that footage using spatial video for viewing in the Vision Pro? Imagine getting a track-level view of a group of Formula 1 cars speeding past at 200 miles per hour with Apple’s depth effect. “[There’s] nothing at this time I can say about it,” said Dickerson.

Recent findings suggest that editors’ note: Jeff Carlson’s travel costs for the F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix were covered by T-Mobile. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A carpet cleaner may not be your first thought for a Black Friday purchase, but it’s actually a great time to buy one, since one of my favorite new cleaners I’ve tested is on sale.
  • The Bissell Little Green cleaner offers tons of cleaning power in a small package at a reasonable price, though there are one or two catches regarding portability and setup that are worth knowing about before you decide which one to buy.
  • The Bissell Little Green Mini is a powerful portable spot cleaner.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A carpet cleaner may not be your first thought for a Black Friday purchase, but it’s actually a great time to buy one, since one of my favorite new cleaners I’ve tested is on sale. The Bissell Little Green Mini Portable Carpet Cleaner is $85 at Amazon, down from its usual $130 price. That’s a $45 savings and, according to Amazon, its lowest price in 365 days. That’s considerably cheaper than the Shark StainForce, which goes for around $200 and is $130 for Black Friday.

The Bissell Little Green cleaner offers tons of cleaning power in a small package at a reasonable price, though there are one or two catches regarding portability and setup that are worth knowing about before you decide which one to buy.

The Bissell Little Green Mini is a powerful portable spot cleaner. / CNET/Ajay Kumar.

The Bissell Little Green Mini is a corded portable spot cleaner, but it’s still lightweight at 7 pounds. Setup is definitely a little more involved, with a clean water tank that you need to mix cleaning solution into and the need to have an AC outlet somewhere in the area. The trade-off is a significantly deeper, more powerful cleaning than what you get with a handheld battery-powered spot cleaner like the Shark StainForce. Using the Little Green on the toughest and oldest dried stains left by my pukey old man cat left me impressed with just how deeply it cleaned my carpets. The pristine result makes this corded cleaner well worth the extra setup, and even at full price ($130), you won’t find fault with its power or portability.

At $85, its lowest price in a year on Amazon, the Bissell Little Green Mini is an easy buy if you have pets and carpet.

Shark StainForce cleaning a stain off my carpet. / Ajay Kumar/CNET.

The Shark StainForce is a unique handheld vacuum because it doesn’t just clean dry messes — it’s primarily intended to remove stains and wet messes. It resembles other handheld vacuums, but comes with a caddy and a custom Shark stain cleaner that mixes a deep cleaner and oxy cleaner in the spray bottle to lift stains.

It works incredibly well — I was blown away by how easily it lifted the worst messes off my white carpets. It removed yellow cat puke stains, wine stains and tomato sauce off both the carpet and couch. It works equally well for older dried stains and wet stains, using a mix of the stain cleaner spray and agitation with the included rubber scrubbing brush head that suctions up the mess at the same time. There’s also a smaller nozzle-brush cleaner included for tight spots.

The StainForce will suction up dry waste like cat hair and chunks of half-digested cat food, but the waste tank is fairly small, and it’s not really meant for dry cleaning of a large area due to the limited battery life.

Industry observers note that the tank will also need to be cleaned out and dried after every use because wet messes will fester and smell if left too long. With all that mentioned, this is the only portable spot cleaner I’ve seen with the design and usability of a handheld vacuum, which makes it an excellent choice if your primary need is portable spot cleaning. The $200 price may sound steep, but I’ve never seen a compact cleaner as good at tackling such tough stains.

I love the Shark StainForce for its service as a grab-and-go cleaner. It’s cordless, it lives in its caddy ready to go, and for a fresh spill I can spray, scrub, and suction in under a minute with no setup at all. I’ve used it on my cats’ worst messes, including hairballs, vomit from eating too fast, and dirty paws tracked in from the litter box. It works remarkably well for something so small and it’s still the go-to cleaner for my wife and I. The dual-spray bottle that comes with it does an incredible job of lifting stains, even from my white carpet.

Sources indicate that here I am scrubbing away with the StainForce powered on. You can still see some stain, but it’s going away.

Recent findings suggest that the Little Green Mini is a different kind of machine, and that difference highlights in the results. On a day when my cats were in rare form and decided to throw up on the bedroom carpet three times in a row, I knew a small portable cleaner like the StainForce wouldn’t cut it, not with the sheer quantity of debris they’d left behind.

Recent findings suggest that I pulled the Bissell Little Green, which, worth acknowledging, is corded. That means more setup: fill the 16-ounce clean tank with water and the included Oxy formula, plug in the 12-foot cord, and work within reach of the cord and its 4-foot hose. It’s still light at just 7 pounds, and it has a useful handle for moving it from room to room.

The StainForce, by contrast, has no clean tank at all. You spray from a separate bottle and only a tiny dirty-water collection tank of under 5 ounces, with about 15 minutes of battery before it needs a recharge. The Mini’s clean and dirty tanks (16 and 13.5 ounces) are much bigger, and because it’s plugged in, it never runs out of power mid-clean.

According to recent reports, that proved to be the lifesaver in cleaning my cat’s horrible messes. The Bissell generously saturated the stain with its built-in sprayer that can dispense water and cleaning solution straight from the hose. The hose digs in deep, rinsing and pulling stains, mess and dirt from deep out of the carpet layers. The larger chunks were safely suctioned into the dirty tank, along with the used water.

According to recent reports, what I can say is that it did an excellent job of deep-cleaning stains from the carpet — noticeably deeper than the StainForce. It completely removed our cat’s mess, with no trace left behind, though our carpets were left a little moist. My wife’s verdict was that she’s never seen the carpets so clean before and she audibly wondered if it was worth investing in a full-size carpet cleaner because clearly the StainForce and vacuuming aren’t cutting it.

Recent findings suggest that if you want the fastest possible cleanup for a fresh spill, get the Shark StainForce; it’s hard to beat a cordless cleaner with zero setup. For a smaller mess that I just want to get off my carpet, the StainForce more than does its job. But if your problem is stains that have soaked into the carpet, the Bissell Little Green Mini is the better cleaner, and at $85 on Black Friday — its lowest Amazon price in a year — it’s $45 less than the StainForce right now. It’s the one I’d buy for a house with pets, kids and carpets where you don’t want a big and bulky carpet cleaner and don’t want to worry about running out of charge for a bigger mess.

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1057 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that grants are one of the best ways you can pay for your education.
  • Grants can be used for tuition, course materials and other cost-of-attendance expenses.
  • Here’s how to use a college grant and what it can pay for.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that grants are one of the best ways you can pay for your education. It’s free money you aren’t expected to pay back.

Grants can be used for tuition, course materials and other cost-of-attendance expenses. Some grants, depending on who awards them, require an application or have requirements you must meet before you can get your money.

Here’s how to use a college grant and what it can pay for.

There are four main types of grants:.

Federal grants come from the federal government.

State grants come from state programs and often can only be used at schools in that state.

Institutional grants come from your college or university, or even your program or major.

Private grants come from nonprofits, community organizations and individual donors.

To receive a federal grant, you must complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA). Most states require the FAFSA for state grants, and a few require a separate state application. You’ll need to complete the FAFSA for each year you’re enrolled in school. You may need to meet certain eligibility requirements, such as income limits, to get some grants. The FAFSA is how you apply for the Pell Grant, which is a financial need-based grant. The FAFSA also determines eligibility for federal work-study, which is a job program rather than a grant.

Recent findings suggest that federal aid, including federal grants, typically requires students to meet satisfactory academic progress. This means you have to maintain a minimum grade point average and be on track to finish your degree on time, as determined by your school. Your school also sets how many credits you must take to qualify for grant funding.

Some grants — typically private or institutional grants — require an additional application that asks for transcripts, letters of recommendation and personal essays. Your school’s financial aid office or the grant provider will have details on applying for specific grants.

After you submit the FAFSA, you’ll receive a financial aid award letter from each school you applied to, which outlines how much in federal, state and institutional grants you’ve been offered. You must accept your aid to receive it.

According to recent reports, most grants will be disbursed directly to your college or university. Your school will apply the grant money first to tuition, fees and any other charges it bills, such as housing or a meal plan.

In some cases, you may receive more grant money than your school bills, which is the best-case scenario. If that happens to you, any leftover funds will likely be refunded to you. Refund timelines vary by school, so it may take some time to get your money. You can get your refund faster by setting up direct deposit with your school. You can then use the funds for other costs approved by your grant — some examples are detailed below.

If you have questions about your grant money, contact your college’s financial aid office.

Recent findings suggest that grants can help cover cost-of-attendance expenses. Generally, you can use grant money to pay for tuition, textbooks, class materials, transportation, housing and food. Depending on your school’s policies, you can use grant money to cover summer classes or study abroad programs, too.

Some grants come with specific terms about how you can spend them. Check your financial aid award letter or, for a private or institutional grant, the school’s or organization’s website to find specifics.

Expenses grants aren’t meant for:.

After your grant is applied to your tuition and school expenses, you can options to fill the gaps between what the grant covers and the total cost of your program. Some options include savings, scholarships, work-study, payment intends, federal student loans or, as a last resort, private loans. By using grants to pay for your college education, you may be able to borrow less.

It has been revealed that to maximize the grants you’re eligible to receive, enter accurate information on the FAFSA and complete it as soon as you can — some funds are first-come, first-served. Also, don’t limit yourself to federal or state grants — search and apply for as many privately funded grants as you can find.

Your grant money usually goes straight to your college or university to pay your tuition and fees. Anything that is left over may be disbursed to you for other school-related costs.

Yes, but it depends on your grant. Housing is part of your cost of attendance, so you can use grant money to pay for off-campus rent.

It has been revealed that you don’t have to pay back a grant as long as you continue to meet all requirements for the grant, such as staying enrolled. You can use grant money on school and school-related expenses. Some grants may require you to meet eligibility requirements such as a minimum GPA or state residency. If you receive more grant money than your cost of attendance for a given school term, ask your financial aid office if you can put that grant money toward next year’s cost of attendance.

If you have a federal grant like a Pell Grant, these are examples when you may have to repay all or part of the grant:.

You withdrew from your program.

You received enough scholarship money to reduce your federal aid need.

Industry observers note that it depends. You can usually use grant money to buy a laptop. Computers are considered course materials, which fall under cost-of-attendance expenses, so they can be covered by a grant. However, always double-check with the grant provider and your financial aid award letter to ensure that you’re following all restrictions. Whether you can use grant money to cover a laptop depends on your school’s policies and how much grant money you receive.

Recent findings suggest that if you get more grant money than your school bills you, you’ll likely receive the leftover money to spend on other cost-of-attendance expenses. You can use this money on living costs such as transportation or housing. Grant money often goes mostly toward tuition, so a refund isn’t guaranteed.

In a recent development, grant and scholarship money is generally tax-free when you use it for tuition, required fees, books and required class supplies. If you have additional questions, consider talking to a tax professional.

Apple Stays Winning as Smartphone Sales Continue to Slump

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (416 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • RAM prices are continuing to put the squeeze on smartphone sales, and even people who typically buy less expensive phones appear to be holding off on upgrading.
  • It has been revealed that according to a new report from Counterpoint Research, smartphone sales in the third quarter of 2026 fell by 9% compared to the same period in 2025.
  • Recent findings suggest that in terms of market share, Samsung held steady at around 25%, while Motorola, Google and other companies saw their slice of the pie decline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

RAM prices are continuing to put the squeeze on smartphone sales, and even people who typically buy less expensive phones appear to be holding off on upgrading.

It has been revealed that according to a new report from Counterpoint Research, smartphone sales in the third quarter of 2026 fell by 9% compared to the same period in 2025. The report attributed the drop to rising memory costs, which are hurting sales at the low end of the Android phone market.

Recent findings suggest that in terms of market share, Samsung held steady at around 25%, while Motorola, Google and other companies saw their slice of the pie decline. Where did those sales go, you might be wondering? Unsurprisingly, Apple’s broad range of iPhone models — from the 17E to its newest foldable flagship, the $1,999 iPhone Duo — bumped the manufacturer’s share of the smartphone market from 50% to 57% since last year.

Recent findings suggest that smartphone-makers with cheaper phone lineups suffered due to component costs, particularly memory, eating into their margins. “There, OEMs have little room to absorb a higher bill of materials without raising prices or cutting volume,” said Counterpoint Senior Analyst Emily Herbert.

The slowdown in phone sales has been happening all year. In the last quarter, the market slumped by 20%, more than was expected at the time. The build-out of data centers to support the ever-expanding AI industry has led to shortages of memory components. In turn, the prices of those components have spiked, raising prices of not just smartphones, but game consoles, PCs and other electronics.

Read more: Best Black Friday iPhone Deals.

Black Friday, Cyber Monday and the Christmas gift-giving season typically mean strong phone sales for companies like Apple and Samsung. But the memory component crisis isn’t going to go away that promptly, and prices of phones are still higher overall.

According to recent reports, counterpoint predicts that smartphone sales will remain weak in the next quarter and that US carriers may be more selective about the promotions they offer this year. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon are also seeing declining sales and customers are getting choosier about committing to phones that often cost more than $1,000. People are also looking to second-hand and refurbished phones instead of buying upcoming.

“Consumers are timing their purchases around the best deals more than ever, if they buy at all,” mentioned Counterpoint Senior Analyst Maurice Klaehne. “This year’s holiday sales cycle will look quite different from usual.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mortgage rates are a little lower this morning, and where they'll go next isn't totally clear.
  • The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage ticked down to 7.05% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow.
  • Inflation data out this morning looks, at first glance, like bad news for mortgage rates.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mortgage rates are a little lower this morning, and where they'll go next isn't totally clear.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage ticked down to 7.05% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is eight basis points lower than yesterday and 33 basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

Inflation data out this morning looks, at first glance, like bad news for mortgage rates. But depending on how markets react, we could actually see lower mortgage rates. Keep reading after the charts for all the details.

Below are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for perspective.

Industry observers note that P.S. Markets will be closed tomorrow for Thanksgiving, and Black Friday's a half day, and mortgage rates don't move much when the markets aren't moving. I won't be here to talk to you about mortgage rates, either, 'cause NerdWallet gives us Thursday and Friday off. Happy Thanksgiving!

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

According to recent reports, mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

Like I mentioned above, it's not totally obvious where mortgage rates will head next. Let's walk through the two scenarios.

In a recent development, here's why rates could go up: This morning, we got October's Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, also known as PCE. It's the last measure of inflation to come out each month, but it's also the Federal Reserve's preferred metric, so PCE gets a lot of attention.

The stats came in mostly as predicted, though it's not like the predictions were good — inflation's been overly strong for a while. But the core year-over-year figure, which came in a tenth of a percent over predictions, could prove troublesome. Core PCE removes categories that can be extra volatile, so it's considered a measure that shows the underlying trend. In this case, the underlying trend is Not Good.

Industry observers note that it's already pretty much a lock that we'll see a rate hike at the Federal Reserve's December meeting, because yes, raising the federal funds rate is the Fed's main tool for taming inflation. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but a rate-hiking cycle from the central bankers definitely keeps upward pressure on borrowing costs.

Industry observers note that on the other hand, here's why that same inflation data could help rates go down: Over the past several days, we've watched the stock market go on a wild ride, with the Anthropic IPO and the return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Yesterday, things weren't looking good for tech stocks, and these inflation numbers could make it even worse.

The amount that tech companies have borrowed to fund AI buildout is a significant concern for investors, since companies will have to cover those costs before investors see any profits. It's already a big task, and if everything costs more thanks to inflation, it's that much harder.

Industry observers note that this AI-related anxiety is rough on the stock market, but it's been a boon for Treasury bonds. More demand for bonds pushes up bond prices, which brings down bond yields (basically, the return investors get on a bond). Mortgage rates for 30-year loans are generally benchmarked to the yield on the 10-year Treasury note, so here's why you care about all of this: Lower Treasury yields means lower mortgage rates, too. If investors keep stressing about inflation eating into tech profits, we could see mortgage rates continue to move lower.

That was a lot of info on inflation, but inflation's not the only major metric influencing rates.

Let's back up for a second. The Federal Reserve tries to keep the economy steady by focusing on two key goals, often referred to as the Fed's dual mandate. One side is price stability — keeping inflation reasonable. The other is maximum employment, meaning those who want to work are able to find jobs.

It has been revealed that next week we'll shift our focus to the employment side of the Federal Reserve's mandate, because the first week of the month is always all about employment data. On Tuesday, Dec. 1, we'll kick things off with the Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS). JOLTS can tip us off to trends in the labor market; stuff like whether folks are leaving jobs voluntarily or if companies have openings that are going unfilled.

It has been revealed that on Wednesday, payroll firm ADP will release its monthly employment stats. ADP is looking at its own payroll data to get an idea of how the job market is growing or contracting. The numbers don't include the public sector, but ADP often provides a preview of how the jobs report will go.

The Employment Situation Summary, better known as the jobs report, drops on Friday. This is the big one, since it tells us the nation's unemployment rate. The jobs report's other major stat is, similar to ADP, how many jobs the economy added or lost in the previous month. Unlike ADP though, the jobs report is inclusive of everybody in the public and private sectors.

Recent findings suggest that lately the labor market's been looking super healthy, which is great news for the economy but less positive for mortgage rates. When hiring's strong, the Fed can feel safer raising the federal funds rate (that's the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers adjust). Higher rates tend to discourage businesses from borrowing and expanding, so if the job market's on shaky footing, the central bankers are going to be cautious about raising the benchmark rate.

What we're seeing now though, where inflation is clearly the problem and employment's just fine, is a recipe for higher rates. Again, the Fed doesn't control mortgage rates, but the central bank being in rate-hike mode puts upward pressure on mortgage rates.

Recent findings suggest that if we were to see employment falter in this latest round of numbers, it still probably wouldn't change the Fed's plan. That would be one poor month for the labor market versus months upon months of inflation running rampant — so yeah, they'll keep an eye on jobs, but inflation's still the scourge.

Our most likely source of lower mortgage rates in the short term is what I described above; investors who are leery of inflation and the promise of AI looking to the safe harbor of the bond market.

» Learn more: How the Fed affects mortgage rates.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you proposal to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you could start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.55% or higher — but there just aren't too many people for whom that's true.

Industry observers note that also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

According to recent reports, if the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

It has been revealed that nerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a newly introduced home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

According to recent reports, » Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

  • Jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex.
  • With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex. Traders, for the moment, must content themselves with the comparatively mundane business of Tuesday's earnings, and options traders are expecting significant moves.

With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.

Recent findings suggest that implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Nvidia vol reached a multi-year high above 92 in the aftermath of President Trump's tariff Liberation day in April '25. In other words, the manufacturer that for much of the AI boom was the most reliable winner in the market, is now more volatile than all but 35 companies in the S&P 500.

"Longer term, I see significant downside risk unless Nvidia can attract an exceptional leader, someone like Tim Cook or AMD's Lisa Su," Nigam Arora, founder of the Arora report, said in a text ahead of the manufacturer's after-market report on Tuesday.

It has been revealed that since hitting all-time highs in October, Nvidia shares have fallen 35%, shedding $2 trillion in market capitalization along the way. Including Nvidia, there are only five companies in the S&P 500 worth more than $2 trillion. However, there is evidence that bulls have been holding out hope while bears snatch up profits: the ratio of open puts to call contracts has actually widened towards calls, according to Barchart data. The ratio is currently 0.87, down from a one-year high of 1.02 two weeks ago and the lowest since the first week of October.

The most popular contract by volume on Monday was the 155-strike put expiring at the bell Monday, but the most popular trade for later expiry was the 160-strike call expiring Thursday, and the second-most-common purchase was the 190-strike call expiring Friday, SpotGamma data show.

According to recent reports, one catch is that most call contracts traded Monday looked like neutral to bearish positions opened by traders selling calls. Of the 5 million options traded on Monday, 3 million were calls, but more were likely opened by sellers than buyers. Of the $2.3 billion in options premium traded on Nvidia Monday, $1.2 billion was tied to puts, SpotGamma data show.

In a recent development, with bears taking profits in puts the past month, there's another potential snag on open interest. There are very few open put contracts at or below the $157 level at which the stock closed Monday. That suggests any bad surprise would find many traders with little downside protection.

By the same token, there's notable open interest in call contracts from the 175-strike and above, suggesting profit-taking on a bounce could limit Nvidia's recovery past levels it breached over the past week.

Either way, Tuesday's earnings could provide fireworks.

Ready for ‘The Great Lock In’? Viral Money Trend Can Improve Focus

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (791 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When it’s cold outside, it’s the ideal time to stay home, organize your finances, set some new money goals and make progress toward them.
  • That’s the promise of the viral winter money trend known as “The Great Lock In” that’s circulating on social media.
  • “You’re probably not doing too much,” notes Robert Baird, wealth manager at Cornerstone Financial Services in Southfield, Michigan.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it’s cold outside, it’s the ideal time to stay home, organize your finances, set some new money goals and make progress toward them.

That’s the promise of the viral winter money trend known as “The Great Lock In” that’s circulating on social media.

“You’re probably not doing too much,” notes Robert Baird, wealth manager at Cornerstone Financial Services in Southfield, Michigan. “It gets dark early. So those can be great months to lock into saving and not spend in excess.”.

One crucial component of the Great Lock In is developing new routines that will last well into 2027, states Jordan Mangaliman, founder and fiduciary wealth advisor at GoldLine Wealth Management in Fullerton, California.

In a recent development, “We want a long-term habit versus a Band-Aid fix,” he states. “In today’s economy, money goes in and out so blindingly fast.”.

Ready to join the movement? Here’s how to get started.

What’s your money moonshot? Maybe it’s paying off all your credit card debt or purchasing a home. Or spending less than you earn. Defining it is the first step toward achieving it.

“Spend a lot of time identifying what that goal is,” Baird claims. “Everyone’s in a different position, so comparing yourself to what you see online might not be applicable.”.

Even while setting ambitious money goals, it’s worth grounding them in reality, Mangaliman says.

If you want to save a larger portion of your income, he suggests trying the latest saving pattern for a couple of months to see how it feels rather than saying you’ll do it forever and then getting frustrated.

“It’s a marathon, not a sprint,” Mangaliman adds.

Once you’ve outlined those significant goals for your Great Lock In, create a budget to help you achieve them, Baird says.

He suggests combing through your previous credit or debit card spending to see where your money is going. Then you can decide what you want to change or shift. Using a tool like the 50/30/20 budget calculator can also help. This approach allots 50% of take-home pay toward needs, 30% toward wants and 20% toward savings and debt payments beyond the minimum.

Baird suggests including saving as a line item in your budget so you don’t forget to do it. “Building that cost into your budget will put you in a better position later,” he states.

Any Great Lock In should include growing your savings, because that makes achieving other goals easier, Baird says.

Recent findings suggest that “Maybe there’s something you could cut in the short term to build up that savings,” he says. Good targets include subscription services, food delivery, entertainment and travel costs.

Saving more is especially challenging in today’s environment, when everyday expenses like gas are higher than they were a year ago.

Baird notes that makes winter a good time to try to reduce costs. There can be fewer temptations to go out and spend money when the days are shorter and the temperatures are colder.

Mangaliman recommends setting aside three to six months’ worth of expenses, although even a smaller amount is helpful. “Ultimately it’s about what you can afford,” he notes. “It’s the foundation of your financial house.”.

Along with building savings, paying down high-interest debt is another pillar of the Great Lock In.

In a recent development, with credit card interest rates higher than they were a few years ago, carrying credit card debt has gotten more expensive. “I would consider applying some savings to paying down debt, especially right now when your debt is costing you more than you can earn in savings,” Baird notes. (You still want to reserve an emergency fund to cover unexpected expenses.).

Industry observers note that “High-interest debt is one of the biggest thieves of wealth,” Mangaliman notes. And one way to avoid turning to debt again in the future is to build up that emergency fund so it’s there for you if you need it.

Even when you are committed to a Great Lock In, some hiccups along the way are inevitable. Success depends on continuing anyway.

According to recent reports, “It’s like a diet,” Baird indicates. “Just because you ate ice cream on a Sunday doesn’t mean on Monday you can’t go right back to being disciplined again.”.

Industry observers note that “Be kind to yourself and do everything in moderation,” Mangaliman suggests. Just wanting to improve your finances is already a great first step, he states.

In fact, he embraces the Great Lock In mentality himself. “There’s an old saying: It’s not how you start, but how you finish,” he says. “And you want to finish the year on a strong note so you carry those habits into 2027 and beyond.”.
